CII 158 micron line serves as most important coolant of interstellar medium in galaxies. Variations occur from object to object. Main emission source at galactic scale remains poorly understood, researchers said.

CII emission compared with neutral gas tracers including CO and HI. CII emission compared with star formation tracers including H-alpha and Spitzer 24 micron data.

CII emission showed striking similarity with H-alpha images when smoothed to same resolution. CII emission showed striking similarity with 24 micron images when smoothed to same resolution. Correlation with neutral gas proved much weaker, scientists said.

CII cooling rate per hydrogen atom increased dramatically across map. Rate measured approximately 2.7 times 10 to negative 26 ergs per second per atom at map border. Rate measured approximately 1.4 times 10 to negative 25 ergs per second per atom in star formation regions.

CII to FIR ratio remained almost constant at two percent. Value exceeded typical quotations by factor of three. Researchers do not believe M31 is unusual, officials said.

Whole-galaxy flux measurements used for comparisons include central regions. CII to FIR ratio known to be lower in central regions. Resolved observations failed to isolate spiral arm. Resolved observations lacked data from outer galactic disk areas. Current observations extend farther into galactic disk.

Researchers examined a two-dimensional tight-binding model of a topological crystalline insulator protected by rotation symmetry. The model stacks two Chern insulators with opposite Chern numbers. The insulators transform under conjugate representations of the rotation group, such as p-plus and p-minus orbitals.

The model resembles the Kane-Mele model. It does not host stable gapless surface states. The model exhibits topological responses. Quantized fractional charge appears bound to rotational defects called disclinations. Angular momentum pumps in response to threading an elementary magnetic flux. A mutual Chern-Simons coupling between the electromagnetic gauge field and an effective gauge field describes these phenomena. The effective gauge field corresponds to rotation symmetry.

The filled bands of the model do not admit a symmetric Wannier representation, researchers reported. This obstruction disappears upon addition of appropriate atomic orbitals. This implies fragile topology. The model response can be derived by representing it as a superposition of atomic orbitals with positive and negative integer coefficients.

The model serves as a prototypical example of two-dimensional topological crystalline insulators protected by rotation. All topological crystalline insulators protected by point group symmetries without protected surface states are either atomic insulators or fragile phases, researchers found. Gapless surface states exist in free electron systems if and only if there is a stable Wannier obstruction.

Researchers used dimensional reduction to map the problem of classifying two-dimensional topological crystalline insulators protected by rotation to a zero-dimensional problem. This mapping yielded the complete non-interacting classification of such topological crystalline insulators. The classification reduces in the presence of interactions. The findings establish fundamental connections between surface states, Wannier obstructions, and topological classification in crystalline systems with rotational symmetry protection.

Scientists measured baryon acoustic oscillation peak in cosmic matter distribution at redshifts up to 3.5. The peak reflects expansion of sonic horizon identified in cosmic microwave background temperature variations.

Researchers achieved measurement accuracy better than 1% using galaxies. Precision reached 1.4-1.6% with Ly-alpha forests and quasar clustering.

Scientists combined BAO measurements with Alcock-Paczynski effect. The AP effect arises from changing ratio of angular to spatial size in spherically-symmetric source distributions at different distances.

BAO measurement ranks among most powerful tools for assessing Universe geometry, officials said.

Study employed five BAO peak measurements from Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV final release. Average redshifts measured at 0.38, 0.51, 0.70, 1.48 and 2.33.

Researchers conducted direct comparison of Lambda-CDM standard model and R_h=ct universe competitor model.

Scientists complemented AP diagnostic with volume-averaged distance probe. The probe assumes constant comoving distance scale r_d.

Both probes contain no uncertain parameters such as Hubble constant. This makes them suited for model selection, researchers said.

R_h=ct showed favor over standard model based solely on AP effect. Likelihood reached 75% versus 25%.

Planck-Lambda-CDM showed favor over R_h=ct based solely on volume-averaged distance probe. Likelihood reached 80% versus 20%.

Joint analysis using both probes produced inconclusive outcome. Both models yielded comparable likelihoods.

Results failed to confirm BAO data support accelerating Universe on their own, researchers said.

The findings appeared in paper analyzing cosmological models. Study focused on geometry of Universe using observational data. Scientists used measurements spanning multiple redshift ranges. Analysis compared competing theoretical frameworks for cosmic expansion. Both models received support from different diagnostic methods. Neither model achieved decisive advantage in combined analysis. Research highlights ongoing debate about Universe acceleration.

Filaments are widespread throughout Galaxy. They host star formation. Reliable detection is essential for understanding star formation process, researchers said.

Team used two versions of UNet-based neural networks for image segmentation. Networks analyzed H2 column density images from Herschel Hi-GAL survey data covering Galactic plane.

Researchers trained networks using filament skeletons extracted from images. Skeletons included spine structures plus branches. Training data also incorporated background masks and missing data masks produced by team.

Eight different training scenarios were tested. Tests determined optimal scenario for classifying pixels as filaments, according to researchers.

Training produced new segmented image of Galactic plane. Image identifies pixels belonging to filamentary structures.

New method classifies significantly more pixels as filaments than input skeleton structures. Increase ranges from factor of two to factor of seven. Range depends on classification threshold applied, team said.

Method reveals previously undetected structures. New structures are primarily low-contrast filaments not identified in earlier surveys, researchers reported.

Team evaluated training scenarios using standard performance metrics. Evaluation demonstrated method robustness. Analysis determined optimal threshold value. Threshold maximizes recovery of input labeled pixel classifications, according to study.

Low-density structures detected for first time. Low-contrast structures also identified that were never seen before. Detection of these structures offers important perspectives for filament studies, researchers said.

Study shows supervised machine learning can reveal filamentary structures present throughout Galactic plane. Method applicable to whole-plane analysis, team concluded.

style_simplified.coling::dc12cc52-6173-4721-b8be-42699b3c: We want to predict how complex systems will act over time. This goal matters in many areas of science. But there is a big problem. We often do not know the rules that control how these systems work. Sometimes we do know the rules. But solving them takes too much time. We need answers faster than that. So people now use a different method. They use machine learning to build models. These models learn from data we collect. They do not need the basic rules. Deep neural networks work this way. Many examples show success with this approach. But there are important questions. Will the model work on new cases? How sure can we be about the results? How much data do we need? People usually answer these questions by using what they already know about the system. We take a different path. We use something called curriculum learning. In curriculum learning, we organize the data in a special way. Training starts with easy examples. Then it moves to harder examples. This order helps the model learn better. It also helps the model work on new problems. People have used this idea before. It works well in robotics. It works well in control systems. We now use this idea for learning about complex systems that change over time. We do this in a careful and complete way. First, we use ideas from ergodic theory. This helps us figure out how much data we need. With enough data, we can promise a good model. We also study how the training data affects predictions far into the future. We look at the structure of the data too. Next, we use entropy as a measure. Entropy tells us how complex the dataset is. We design the training set using entropy analysis. This design makes the models much better. The models work well on new cases. We also give guidance about data. We explain how much data you need. We explain which data to choose. This makes data-driven modeling more effective.
style_simplified.coling::7876816d-0ac2-4404-b2bf-deeaa0b7: The CII 158 microns line is the most important coolant of the interstellar medium in galaxies. Different objects show substantial variations. The main source of the emission at a galactic scale is still poorly understood. Previous studies of the CII emission in galaxies have a resolution of several kpc or more. The observed emission is an average of different ISM components. The aim of this work is to study the CII emission at the scale of a spiral arm. This is the first time this has been done. We want to investigate the origin of this line. We also want to study its use as a tracer of star formation. We present CII and OI observations of a segment of a spiral arm of M~31. We used the Infrared Space Observatory. The CII emission is compared with tracers of neutral gas. These tracers are CO and HI. The emission is also compared with tracers of star formation. These tracers are H alpha and Spitzer 24 mu. The similarity of the CII emission with the Ha and 24 mu images is striking when smoothed to the same resolution. The correlation with the neutral gas is much weaker. The CII cooling rate per H atom increases dramatically from about 2.7e-26 ergs per second per atom in the border of the map to about 1.4e-25 ergs per second per atom in the regions of star formation. The CII to FIR ratio is almost constant at 2 percent. This is a factor 3 higher than typically quoted. However, we do not believe that M~31 is unusual. The whole galaxy fluxes used for the comparisons include the central regions. The CII to FIR ratio is known to be lower there. The resolved observations neither isolate a spiral arm nor include data as far out in the galactic disk as the observations presented here. A fit to published PDR models yields a plausible average solution. The solution is G0 of about 100 and n of about 3000 for the PDR emission in the regions of star formation in the arm of M31.
style_simplified.coling::1a16d27a-89fc-4df9-8b4f-cf2532a8: We look at a flat model of a special insulator. The model has two dimensions. The insulator is special because it has a certain symmetry. That symmetry involves rotation. We build the model by putting two layers on top of each other. Each layer is a Chern insulator. The two layers have opposite Chern numbers. They transform in different ways under rotation. They use orbitals like p plus and p minus orbitals. The model looks similar to another model. That other model is called the Kane-Mele model. But our model is different in one way. It does not have stable states on its surface. Those surface states would have no energy gap. Even so, the model shows topological responses. One response is the appearance of fractional charge. This charge is quantized. It is bound to rotational defects. Those defects are called disclinations. Another response is the pumping of angular momentum. This happens when you thread an elementary magnetic flux through the system. These responses are described by a coupling. The coupling is a mutual Chern-Simons coupling. It involves the electromagnetic gauge field. It also involves an effective gauge field. That effective field corresponds to the rotation symmetry. We also show something about the filled bands. They do not admit a symmetric Wannier representation. But you can remove this obstruction. You do this by adding appropriate atomic orbitals. This means the topology is fragile. Because of this, we can derive the response. We represent the model as a superposition. It is a superposition of atomic orbitals. The orbitals have positive and negative integer coefficients. After analyzing this model, we show a general result. All such insulators protected by point group symmetries are either atomic insulators or fragile phases. This is true if they do not have protected surface states. We then use dimensional reduction. This maps the problem to zero dimensions. We use this to obtain the complete classification.

We introduce a new artificial intelligence approach. We call it the Digital Synaptic Neural Substrate. We also call it DSNS. It uses selected attributes from objects in various domains. These domains include chess problems. They include classical music. They include renowned artworks. The system takes these attributes. It recombines them in a special way. This generates new attributes. These new attributes can then be used to create novel objects. These objects have creative value to humans. They relate to any one of the source domains. This allows some of the burden of creative content generation to be passed from humans to machines.

The approach was tested in the domain of chess problem composition. We used it to automatically compose numerous sets of chess problems. These were based on attributes extracted and recombined from chess problems. They also used tournament games by humans. They used renowned paintings. They used computer-evolved abstract art. They used photographs of people. They used classical music tracks. The quality of these generated chess problems was then assessed automatically. We used an existing computational chess aesthetics model. This model had been experimentally validated. The problems were also assessed by human experts in the domain.

The results suggest that attributes collected and recombined from chess and other domains using the DSNS approach can indeed be used. They can automatically generate chess problems of reasonably high aesthetic quality. In particular, a low quality chess source used in combination with actual photographs of people was able to produce three-move chess problems. These problems had comparable quality or better to those generated using a high quality chess source. The high quality source was published compositions by human experts. The combination was also more efficient. Why information from a foreign domain can be integrated and functional in this way remains an open question for now. The DSNS approach is scalable. It is applicable to any domain in which objects have attributes. These attributes can be represented using real numbers.

Scientists see a special pattern in space. This pattern is called the BAO peak. It appears in how matter spreads through the universe. We can see this pattern at distances that show us the universe long ago. The pattern comes from sound waves that traveled through the early universe. These same waves show up in the cosmic microwave background. That background is ancient light from when the universe was very young.

Scientists can now measure where this peak sits very precisely. They use galaxies to do this. They get accuracy better than one percent. They also use other objects called quasars. They use something called Ly-alpha forests too. With these they get slightly less accuracy.

There is another effect scientists study. It is called the AP effect. This effect happens because distances look different in different directions as you go farther away. Objects that are really round look stretched or squashed from far away.

Together these measurements help scientists understand the shape of the universe. They help test different theories about how the universe works.

In this paper scientists used five measurements. The measurements came from a big survey called Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV. The measurements were from five different distances into space and time.

The scientists compared two theories. One theory is the standard model. It is called Lambda-CDM. The other theory is called the R_h=ct universe. This second theory competes with the standard model.

The scientists used two different ways to test the theories. One way favored the R_h=ct theory. It gave it seventy-five percent likelihood. The standard model got twenty-five percent. The other way favored the standard model. It gave it eighty percent likelihood. The R_h=ct theory got twenty percent.

When both tests were combined the result was unclear. Both theories looked equally good. So this work cannot prove that the universe is speeding up its expansion.

Background. Long thin clouds are everywhere in our Galaxy. Stars are born inside these clouds. We need to find these clouds in a good way. This helps us learn how stars are born.

Goals. We want to see if computers can learn to find these long thin clouds. We want to search the whole flat disk of our Galaxy.

How We Did It. We used two computer programs. These programs look at pictures and sort them into groups. We gave the programs special pictures to study. The pictures show gas in our Galaxy. A space telescope called Herschel took these pictures. We marked the long thin clouds in these pictures. We drew lines to show where the clouds are. These lines showed the main path of each cloud. They also showed the side branches. We also marked areas with no data. We marked background areas too. We tried eight different ways to train the computers. We wanted to find the best way to sort pixels into the cloud group.

What We Found. The trained computers made a new picture of our Galaxy. In this new picture, pixels that belong to long thin clouds are marked. This new way finds many more pixels. It finds two to seven times more pixels than our original marked lines showed. The exact number depends on our choice of cutoff value. The computers found new clouds. These are mostly faint clouds. They are hard to see. Nobody had found them before. We used common tests to check how well each training method worked. These tests prove our method works well. The tests also helped us pick the best cutoff value. This value gives us the best match with our original marked pixels.

Summary. This early test shows that computer learning can find long thin clouds across our whole Galaxy. Finding these clouds is important. This includes faint clouds that we never saw before. This discovery will help us study these clouds much better.
style_simplified.coling::f4961832-eeb4-41fc-8a64-82c30107: I want to say first that I do like Cowboy Bebop. The animation looks great. The designs look great. The music is fantastic. I live in New Zealand. People say we are in the middle of a very important election right now. They say it is one of the most important elections our country has ever had. I am not planning to vote. The electoral commission is running campaigns. These campaigns try to encourage everyone to vote. I think these campaigns are stupid.

Many people around me care about politics. These people do not seem to understand something. Some people simply do not have a view. Helen Clark's government ended. Then John Key came in. Did that really affect me? Not really. Actually, it did not affect me at all. Labour might win this year. Will that affect me? I do not really think so. I will continue doing what I do. People will continue to hate the government. A couple of terms will pass. Then National will come back in. It will still have no real effect on my daily life.

I have an opinion because of this. I really do not care. It is not worth my time to research. Research might make me care. I should leave the voting to other people. Those people know what they are talking about. That is fine. This attitude is generally accepted here.

Recently something has changed. There has been a whole lot of guilting. People are being guilted into voting. There are campaigns with slogans. One slogan says this: "It's only democracy if you vote, idiot." I have seen some extreme ones too. One had a picture of the earth. The earth was decaying. It was something about climate change. Next to it was just a huge block letter. The letter said "VOTE."

I might mention something to my friends. I might say I am not planning on voting. Half of my friends would be fine with it. The other half would grill me alive. They would say I am not contributing to my country's future. This guilt makes people feel something. They feel they need to vote. They obviously do not know who to vote for. So they are easily vulnerable to manipulation.

Just yesterday I saw a flyer. It was in one of my lectures. It had information on each party's policies. Except it was not really a fair description. It had colour coding. The colours showed which policies were good. But good according to whose opinion? It basically stacked up left to right. It showed that right is evil. It showed that left is good.

The green party also came in. They offered free bus passes. These passes were for outside of peak hours. They were for university students. This is the most moronic policy in the universe. It achieves nothing in the real world. But it gets a bunch of voters converted. I am sure the right wing is doing it too. The left is more apparent to me. This is because I am a university student.

So here is my conclusion. People should not be encouraged to vote. They should be encouraged not to vote. This applies if they do not know what they are talking about. People will vote for all the wrong reasons. Politics becomes open to extreme manipulation of voters.

The electoral commission is guilting people into voting. There is only one reason for this. They are all interested in politics. They do not realize something. A lot of people just quite simply do not care. It is like forcing the entire country to watch the rugby. Honestly, the All Blacks losing would have a bigger effect on me. A change in government would have less effect.

style_simplified.coling::17ad7e76-2fa1-4c9b-a42b-44a53287: I am not sure what I think about this issue. But I will start by arguing against gay marriage. I have two reasons for this. First, I lean less toward the side I am starting with. That side seems much more fragile. That side is also less popular. Arguing for a weaker position helps me practice. It helps me get better at making arguments. I feel less strongly about this position. Second, I believe one side has the burden of proof. The side that favors gay marriage has that burden. I will explain why. Please watch this video. The video is only two minutes long. The video makes an argument. Because of that argument, I feel one side must prove its case. Some people want to redefine marriage. Those people want to change what marriage means. They must prove why we should change it. I do not have problems with changing definitions. But changing a definition requires a good reason. You need a compelling reason. People sometimes answer a question. The question is this: "Do you think gay marriage is a good idea?" They answer by saying "Why not?" This answer is a fallacy. It is called the teapot fallacy. They are trying to shift the burden of proof. That is not fair. I do not believe equality is a good argument here. People with different sexual orientations deserve equal rights. They deserve the right to life. They deserve liberty. They deserve freedom. They deserve the pursuit of happiness. The constitution details these rights. However, the equality argument is a red herring in this case. A red herring means it distracts from the real issue. Marriage is not a privilege. Marriage is not a right that must be equal for all types of relationships. Marriage is an institution. It was built around having children. It was built around procreation. Homosexual relationships may be loving. They may be committed. But by definition they cannot produce children. They are non-procreational. Some heterosexual marriages also cannot produce children. Old couples cannot have children. Infertile couples cannot have children. But if you watched the video, you will understand something. These cases are not the same. Just because there are exceptions does not mean you can extend the definition. The exceptions do not define the norm. The norm is not defined by its exceptions. This equality issue is not the same as women voting. It is not the same as black people being free. People often present criteria as a question. The question is this: "If two people love each other, why shouldn't they be able to get married?" Marriage criteria have nothing to do with love. They have nothing to do with romantic love either. If your criteria are two individuals who have romantic love, then incest is fair game. If your criteria are two individuals who have sexual love, then incest is also fair game. Some will argue that incest is different. They say there are power issues within the family. They say there are genetic defects. But there can be power issues within any relationship. Power issues can happen in heterosexual relationships. They can happen in homosexual relationships. They can happen in incestuous relationships. There is no reason to base marriage laws on this. Also, incestuous couples do not have to have children. They can adopt children. They may be infertile. They may be homosexual. One may argue that incest should be a valid form of marriage. One may argue it should be valid just like homosexuality. You can try to argue this point if you want. But please include valid reasoning. The burden of proof is on you. The argument "why would you care?" is invalid. Just because something does not affect anyone badly does not mean we can change institutions at whim. We cannot change things whenever we want. Even under utilitarianism, this argument does not work. Gay people can have fulfilling relationships. These can be long-term relationships. They can be romantic relationships. They can be sexual relationships. They do not need to call it marriage. Redefining marriage for the happiness of a group is similar to something else. It is like giving in to lobbyist demands. We give in so they will be happier. This is similar logically. It is not similar emotionally. Most arguments for gay marriage are appeals to emotion. They are appeals to popularity. The term "gay rights" was designed to make it sound like we have camps for them. Like we have internment camps. Even the term "homophobe" was created to stigmatize the opposition. This issue is popular in our time. Many opponents are religious fundamentalists. They use bad arguments. They use straw man arguments. But that does not make the other side correct. It does not make the "more reasonable side" right. Imagine a movement to legalize incestuous marriage. Imagine it was popular. There would be videos online. There would be websites online. They would glorify the struggle of such couples. Most people would be for that as well. Why is one sexual deviation more acceptable for marriage than another? I mean to use that term with complete respect. I mean absolutely no stigma. I mean no negative connotation. I mean no negative implication. My view changed. In all fairness, I was already seventy-five percent there when I wrote this.
style_simplified.coling::bd4df89c-701f-407b-9fc6-2c51aa5b: I am talking about one kind of blame. Some users of rpolitics say this. Some members of OWS say this. Hamilton Nolan from Gawker says this. I will put their view in my own words. Here is what they believe: Our system lets some people get much more money than others. That fact alone is wrong. If you do get a lot of money in this system, you are probably a bad person. Hedge fund managers sit around. They spend tens of millions of dollars on dead sharks in tanks. Do they not know something important? A tiny bit of their daily earnings would help others a lot. It would pay off the student loans of an average redditor. That is just one example. I have heard this bad argument many times. I have heard it from activists. I have heard it from internet commenters. These people come from the middle class. Some come from the working class. They live in advanced Western countries. But here is the thing. You also have much more than most people in the world. You could save one hundred dollars. You could skip upgrading your smartphone. You could walk home in the rain. You would not take a cab. You could eat lentils for a few weeks. You could eat beans for a few weeks. You could skip buying that new piece of clothing you wanted. Then you could donate that one hundred dollars. That money would save the lives of dozens of kids. Those kids would otherwise die of Malaria. Is your comfort more important than other people's lives? Is your convenience more important? Is your entertainment more important? I will not accept certain excuses. Do not say that charities might not use the money well. Do not say that charitable donations could hurt local industry over time. For this discussion, we must agree on something. We must agree that wealth could be moved around. That moving of wealth would help the people who receive it. We must also agree on something else. The average American wants to donate to a worthy cause. He wants to donate in a way that truly helps. He would be able to do so. I do not think these ideas are crazy. So here is my view. Some people attack the rich. They attack them only because they are rich. Those people are hypocrites. They ignore their own place in the world economy. They are relatively well off. They believe the wealth of others should be spread around. This would reduce inequality. But they are hypocrites. They do not spread around their own wealth. That would also reduce inequality. Now I do not donate much to charity myself. But I do not think people richer than me are evil by nature. I can see what my choices reveal. I would rather upgrade to business class. I would not save five hundred lives in a developing country. That is my preference. Some billionaire would rather upgrade his yacht. He would not dissolve all his assets. He would not use that money to promote communism. I do not really blame him. Many people disagree with me. A top Saudi military official made a different claim. He said weeks of airstrikes had made the Shiite group much weaker. The rebel leader is Abdul-Malik al-Houthi. He spoke on television. He said his fighters would not leave the main cities. He said they would not leave the government buildings. He added more words. He said anyone who thinks they will surrender is dreaming. He made his comments after more than three weeks of bombings. A coalition led by Saudi Arabia has been doing the bombings. The goal is to push back the Houthis. The Houthis surged into the capital city in January. The capital is called Sanaa. They forced out the President. His name is Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi. Hadi still says he is the real leader of Yemen. He is working with the Saudis to return to his country. He has other allies too. The violence started in mid-March. More than seven hundred people have been killed since then. The violence shows no sign of slowing down. These numbers come from the World Health Organization. The Houthis say the people of the country support them. Al-Houthi spoke on Sunday. He said it is the right of the Yemeni people to stand against the attacks. They can use all possible means. This is true as long as the attacks continue. He said more. He said his people will move and react against the attacks. He mentioned the killing of children and women. He said he does not want to hear any voices and cries after that. But there are signs of some breaking apart. This is among forces loyal to a former President. His name is Ali Abdullah Saleh. Many of these forces have fought alongside the rebels. One general is AbdulRahman AlHalili. He leads more than ten thousand troops. He has now joined with Hadi. Military sources said this on Sunday. A Saudi general spoke on Sunday too. His name is Ahmed Asiri. He is a brigadier general. He said airstrikes had destroyed much of the Houthis' central command. They did this by targeting their communications. He said the rebels are now in a defensive stance. They are in areas under siege. The campaign is called Operation Decisive Storm. It began on March twenty-six. The coalition has launched two thousand three hundred airstrikes. Asiri said this. CNN reporters Don Melvin and Christine Theodorou helped with this report.
style_simplified.coling::ef2146c2-c9fe-4563-b26a-b39f1bb9: This is the very loud moment when a mother finds out she will have a girl. She already has six boys. She tried seven times to have a girl. A video shows the woman. Her name is Cher Lair. She lives in Apex. That town is in North Carolina. She cuts into a cake at a party. Her family stands around her. The party is to show if the baby is a boy or a girl. She did not know what the baby would be. She gave her scan papers to a baker. The baker looked at the papers. The woman cuts the cake. She lifts up one slice. The cake inside is pink. Pink means girl. She cannot believe what she sees. Her eyes go wide. She screams very loud. She is so excited. She falls backward because she is so surprised. Then she gets down on her knees. She says the same thing over and over. She pants and says: 'Oh my God.' People stand nearby and watch. They cheer for her. They clap their hands. They are happy too. They watch everything happen. Lair talked to a television station. The station is called WTVD. She said she had given up. Her husband is named Stephen. He had given up too. They thought they would never have a daughter. She said she thought about it with baby three. She thought about it with baby four. She thought a girl would come at some point. She thought they could not all be boys. But then came baby four. Then came baby five. Then came baby six. After that she started thinking differently. She thought maybe they could all be boys. The mother of six boys learned the news on Monday. She learned she would have a little girl. A friend helped her. The friend was told if the baby was a boy or a girl. The friend helped bake the cake. The cake was chocolate. The inside was colored pink. Lair says she feels nervous. A girl will enter a house full of boys. But she feels excited too. She wants to do mother and daughter things together. She wants to take her daughter to see Cinderella. She wants to get pedicures together. Pedicures make your toenails pretty. She wants to get manicures together. Manicures make your fingernails pretty. She wants to shop for a prom dress one day. The video has been watched many times. More than one hundred thousand people have seen it. Many viewers like the video. One person wrote a comment. The comment said the video is awesome. The comment said the little girl is lucky. She will have six big brothers. The brothers will look after her. The person said congratulations. Lair will have her seventh child in August. Nobody knows yet what names they are thinking about.

A famous rap group called Migos got arrested during their tour. The police found drugs and guns in their van. This happened when they were playing a show at a college. The three rappers are Quavious Marshall, Kirschnick Ball, and Kiari Cephus. Quavious Marshall is 24 years old. Kirschnick Ball is 20 years old. Kiari Cephus is 23 years old. The police took them away on Saturday night. They were in the middle of their show. The show was at Georgia Southern University. The police took them to jail right away.

A judge said they cannot leave jail. The judge denied their bond. This means they must stay locked up. They may miss their other concerts. They were supposed to play more shows soon. Their next show was at a place called Ksu Convocation Center. That place is in Georgia. After that they planned to go to other states. They were going to Wisconsin. They were going to Ohio. They were going to Michigan. They were going to Pennsylvania. They were going to New York.

The police smelled something strong. The smell was coming from two big tour buses. The smell was marijuana. Marijuana is a drug. The police thought the rappers had drugs with them. The rappers went inside to do their concert. The concert was at a place called Hanner Fieldhouse arena. While the rappers performed, the police searched the buses. They found many guns inside. They found marijuana inside. They found another drug too. The police did not say what that other drug was.

The police were very worried. They said the discoveries were very concerning. The rappers brought these things to a college event. More than a thousand students were at this event. The students were all gathered together there.

The three rappers are famous. They made a popular song in 2013. That song was called Versace. They made another popular song in 2014. That song was called Fight Night. The police arrested them after they finished performing. They walked off the stage and got arrested.

The rappers face serious charges now. They are charged with having drugs. They are charged with having guns at a school. They are charged with having guns while doing a crime. Nobody knows if they have lawyers yet. The Associated Press tried to contact their managers. They called and sent emails. The managers did not answer back.

About twelve other people got arrested too. These people were in the two vans. The police took them to jail after the concert. We do not know what charges they face yet.

This concert was a special event. The school has this concert every spring. Migos had a deal with Georgia Southern. The deal was to perform at this event. The group started making music together in 2009.

A teenager has died. He fell off the roof of a building. The building was in the Bronx. The building had six stories. He was running away from police officers. The police were there because of complaints. People had complained about a group. The group was smoking marijuana. The group was also loitering.

Hakeem Kuta was 17 years old. He was on life support. He passed away on Saturday morning. This happened around 11am. He had injuries from the fall. The fall happened on Thursday night. The New York Police Department said this.

Police said Kuta was a junior. He went to Bronx Envision Academy. He seemed to have made a mistake about a ledge. He was backing away from police officers who were coming toward him.

Hakeem Kuta fell six stories. He fell from the roof of the Bronx building. This happened on Thursday.

Police were answering complaints. The complaints were about a group of teens. The teens were smoking marijuana. They were also loitering in the lobby. Kuta ran when police officers arrived. Five others also ran. This is what police said.

The 17-year-old jumped over a wall. The wall was three feet high. Then he fell six stories. He fell from the building.

Officers had chased Kuta. They also chased five other teenagers. They chased them up the stairs. There had been complaints. The complaints said they were smoking marijuana. This was in the lobby of the building. The building was on Valentine Avenue. Valentine Avenue is in Mott Haven. A spokesman said this. His name is Stephen Davis.

The officers got to the roof. Some teens jumped to another roof. They ran away. However, Kuta did not get away. His companion also did not get away. The companion was 14 years old. He has not been named. They were pinned in by a wall. The wall divided the area.

Police said Kuta jumped over a wall. The wall was three feet high. He did not realize something. There was a gap between the buildings.

His friend tried to help. The friend held onto his jacket. He held on desperately. Kuta was dangling. He was 60 feet from the ground. Below him was an alleyway.

Officers got to the roof. Some teens jumped and ran away. However, Kuta was pinned in. His companion who was 14 years old was also pinned in. A wall divided the area and pinned them in.

Hakeem was taken to a hospital. The hospital was St Barnabas Hospital. He was listed in critical condition. He died around 11am on Saturday.

Officer Edmundo Rivera grabbed the companion. This kept him from falling over the edge. But the friend lost his grip on Kuta. Kuta fell from the roof. He fell six stories. He fell to the pavement.

Police ran to where he fell. He fell in the courtyard. Kuta was then taken to the hospital.

His father is Munir Kuta. Munir is 42 years old. He is an immigrant. He came from Ghana. He said his son stayed out of trouble. He said his son does not do drugs. He said it is not easy. He said his son was a nice kid.

Authorities said something. There most likely would not have been any arrests. They only wanted the teens to stop smoking marijuana.

No tickets were given out. However, marijuana was found. It was found in the lobby.

A policewoman from China fought a bad man. The man had a big knife. She used only her hands. She got hurt during the fight. The woman is 22 years old. Her name is Cao Yu. She had no weapon. She stopped the man for five minutes. This happened in a public square. The square is in Guizhou province. This province is in southwestern China. It happened earlier this month.

The man was in his twenties. He was holding two knives. He stabbed her in the shoulder. She had confronted him. She was on patrol at the time. The People's Daily Online reported this story. You can scroll down for video.

Chinese social media users praised Cao Yu. They called her a tough girl. They said she was incredibly brave.

The 22-year-old confronted the man. He was waving around a machete. This happened in a public square. The square is in south west China.

She continued to fight with him. He had the machete in his hands. The machete was 60 centimeters long. She got more wounds. Both hands were wounded. Then her colleagues arrived. They brought the man under control.

The young policewoman was bleeding all over. Someone found her that way. She is now recovering in hospital. The incident was horrific.

Ms Cao said something. She said she could not let the man hurt innocent people.

The knife was 60 centimeters long. It caused terrible cuts. The policewoman was unarmed. She was 22 years old. The thug also held another small knife.

She added more in an interview. The interview was with a local television station. She was trying to take over the machete. She wanted to stall him. She waited until another officer came. She needed help from that officer. There were a lot of tourists. They were walking around the square. She needed to make sure they were safe.

The man is thought to have robbed someone. That person was a passer by. Ms Cao saw him do this.

The wounds were bloody. They were on Cao Yu's shoulder. They were also on her right hand. The machete struck her and caused these wounds.

Mr Cao is getting medical treatment. The treatment is in the local hospital. This happened after fighting off the robber.

Jiao Chun is one of the policemen. He arrived on the scene. He said something. Their colleagues asked the man to drop his machete. He did not drop it. He kept saying something. He wanted to rob someone for more money.

Chinese social media users have praised Ms Cao. They praised her extraordinary bravery. CCTV footage was released this week. The footage showed the whole incident.

One user posted on Weibo. Weibo is the Chinese equivalent of Twitter. The user said she is a real tough girl. Those who say they are so tough every single day are not tough at all.

Another user asked why an armed police officer was not sent immediately. They wanted someone to deal with the incident. Where are the qualified policemen? Are we too shorthanded? Can we send an armed policeman? Can we send a well trained policeman to fight the bad guy?

These are two different questions. Let me explain.

Bridge: The Atlantic Ocean is very big. It is really really big. The size depends on where you cross. It can be bigger than the whole USA. The ocean is wet. It gets storms. Water and storms can damage concrete. They can damage steel too. You would need concrete and steel to build a bridge. The ocean is too deep. You cannot sink poles down to the bottom. The poles would hold up the bridge. But they cannot reach that far down. The ocean has many storms. It has big waves. You could try a floating bridge instead. That is called a pontoon bridge. But the waves would shake it. The bridge would break into pieces. The ocean is big. The ocean is empty. Not many people would want to drive across it. The drive would be very boring. Cars need fuel. They could not carry enough fuel for the whole trip.

Here is more detail. We cannot sink poles to hold the bridge steady. The materials we have cannot handle a floating bridge. The stress would be too much. Salt water causes rust. The air near the ocean also causes rust. Fixing the bridge would be very hard. You would need fuel on the crossing. Someone would have to ship fuel to the middle of the ocean. That does not make sense.

Tunnel: The Atlantic is very deep. There is lots of water above the ocean floor. All that water creates pressure. It pushes down on the bottom. Think about diving in a pool. Your ears hurt when you go deep. Now multiply that feeling by ten thousand times. That is how much pressure exists down there. They could try to dig a tunnel. But the tunnel could never spring a leak. Not even a tiny leak. If it did leak, the walls would fall down. Everyone inside would drown. You would need big fans. Very big fans. The fans would move air through the tunnel. Everyone needs air to breathe. You would have the fuel problem again too.

Here is more detail. The real problem is the joints. Workers would make tunnel sections ahead of time. Then they would put the sections into place. The sections would connect together. But the joints where they connect would not be strong enough. The pressure is too great. Even small leaks would be dangerous. Water under that much pressure cuts like a laser. It cuts like a laser in movies. Ventilation is another huge problem. The tunnel would be thousands of miles long. The air inside would be dead air. It would not move. You would need to circulate it somehow. Otherwise you could not make it through alive. Fuel is a problem here as well.

No, it cannot be done. The ocean is too big. It is too deep. It is too rough.

Someone found information about this idea. Is the tunnel possible? Maybe it is possible. Early engineers in the eighteen hundreds thought about space travel. They thought it might be possible someday. If enough scientists want this tunnel, it might get built. If enough politicians want it, it might get built. They would have to really want it. Otherwise, it will not happen.

Ask yourself some questions. Why would anyone want to drive across the Atlantic? What good would a bridge or tunnel do? Who would pay to build it? How would they get their money back? Who would take care of it after it was built? It would be in international waters. No country owns international waters. What country would be responsible? What local government would handle it? Who would manage the utilities? Who would manage the infrastructure? It is not realistic. It is not practical. It is not needed.

Tunnel: Here is another point. Most people have not mentioned this point. But it is important. The Mid Atlantic Ridge runs through the ocean. The Atlantic Ocean is pulling itself apart. It pulls apart at a rate of two and a half centimeters each year. You would have to deal with volcanoes. You would have to deal with earthquakes. Look at a map of the ocean floor. You can see what it looks like without water.

Even if someone builds a tunnel, would it be useful? Think about your car. How far can it travel before it needs more fuel? How many hours can you drive before you get too tired? What if something bad happens in the middle of the tunnel? Emergency workers would be hours away. It would take hours for them to reach you.

Yes, it is possible. We have the technology now. But it is not economically viable. The cost would be extremely high. The benefit would be very small. The project might become more realistic in the future. Technology will improve over the coming decades.

Sometimes there are not many athletes in one category. There are not enough athletes to fill up a whole race. When this happens, they run similar categories together. Athletes with less affected cerebral palsy can ride with athletes who have amputations that affect them less. But they are only scored in their own class. They do this at most bike races. It speeds things up. It consolidates the races.

The Paralympics have a complicated system. They use classifications and adjustments. They try to keep things as fair as possible. There are not a lot of disabled athletes. There is a wide variety of disabilities. Different disabilities give different advantages and disadvantages. For example, look at wheelchair sports. Amputees often have an advantage over people who are paralyzed. Amputees are lighter. Amputees are more able to move around. Sometimes they need to have enough people to hold a competition. They have to accept that some disability types will have an advantage. This is not really different from the regular Olympics. Tall people have an advantage in basketball. No one is trying to fix that.

The categories are based on what the disability causes. They are not based on the type of disability. Look at cycling. One category is for people with upper body disabilities. Another category is for people with one limb disability who can pedal with both legs. Another category is for people with a leg injury who only pedal with one leg. The last category is for people with both legs affected. If cerebral palsy affects the legs of an athlete, they would be put in the last category. Someone else with another disability that affects both legs would go there too. The athletes must be classified internationally. This requires an examination. The examination shows how the disability affects the athlete. This helps ensure that people cannot game the system. People cannot get placed in a category for more disabled athletes.
style_simplified.coling::5895f991-9d37-49fe-9f39-eeff324a:
Some animals do not just play dead. They also make bad smells. The bad smells make predators think the meat has gone rotten. Not all predators can eat rotten meat. The predator will leave the animal alone. The predator will look for safer food instead.

Many predators cannot understand tricks. They do not think about whether something might be fooling them.

Animals that seem sick get avoided by predators. This makes sense. A sick animal might make the predator sick too. The sickness could even kill the predator. Playing dead might look simple. But the predator must think about risks. The predator worries about bacteria. The predator worries about viruses. The predator worries about other bad things.

Think about defending yourself from an attacker. Your body fills with adrenaline. You fight back very hard. You act crazy to protect yourself. Then the attacker stops moving. The danger seems over now. You start to feel safe again. It does not matter why they stopped. Maybe they are unconscious. Maybe they are dead. Maybe they are faking. You still feel safer. And you are a human. You can think and reason. Animals just follow instinct.

Prey animals have instincts to protect themselves. They trample attackers. They headbutt attackers. They bite attackers. They use horns to gore attackers. They use antlers to gore attackers. But once the threat stops moving, the instinct goes away. The prey animal loses interest.

Hunting animals work the same way. They see prey running away. They see prey moving around. This triggers their aggression. The movement makes them want to attack. When the prey stops moving, they lose interest. They only care about feeding if they feel hungry.

Take a bear as an example. A bear shows territorial aggression. A bear shows defensive aggression. The bear loses interest when the crisis ends. Playing dead works on a bear.

But this trick does not work on all predators. Think about a pack of wolves. Wolves want to eat you. When you stop struggling, they think dinner is ready. They start eating right away.
style_simplified.coling::a9b058a8-5ce8-448f-820a-6ffba640:
The reason is the camera's field of view. People call this FOV. Some people play first person shooter games. Those people know about FOV. Some people know about cameras. Those people also know about FOV. Think about what you can see. It starts at your eye. It goes out in a cone shape. You can see a picture of this at URL0. FOV is an angle. It is the angle between the two sides of the cone. Players in shooter games often make the FOV bigger. This gives them an advantage. They can see more around them. There is an example at URL1. I found it on the internet. It shows what happens when you increase FOV in a game. The left image has FOV expanded to sixty five degrees. The default is forty five degrees. That is on the right. The larger FOV lets you see more. You see more on the left side. You see more on the right side. But notice something else. The two trailer things look farther away. The player is standing in the same place. This happens because you increased the FOV. The light from distant objects changes. It converges on your flat surface differently. A larger FOV makes objects shrink faster. They shrink as they get farther away. The opposite is also true. You can decrease the FOV. Then far away objects look bigger. They converge on a larger part of the view area. The camera on DSCOVR has a very small FOV. It is only zero point six one degrees. This makes it very good at collecting light from far away objects. It focuses on a very small cone. The distance between Earth and Moon matters less with this camera. It does not affect their relative size the same way. Regular cameras show size differently. Human eyes also show size differently.

Now hold your hand in front of your face. It is probably about as big as your monitor. Keep your hand in the same spot. Move your head backwards. Your hand now looks smaller than the monitor. There is a certain distance where things change. Your hand gets smaller. The monitor gets smaller. They get smaller together. They shrink at the same rate. This happens for a reason. The distance between you and those two things becomes much greater. It is much greater than the distance between those two things. Angular diameter depends on distance. It also depends on ratio of distances. The first image is very close to the moon. It is far from the earth. So the moon seems big. The second image is very far from both. It is far from the earth. It is far from the moon. So they appear like their actual relative sizes. The earth does appear smaller in the second image. But the moon got smaller much faster. It is just like your hand.

DSCOVR had its camera zoomed in more. The camera is called EPIC. It is on the spacecraft. It took the image. It is designed to observe Earth from a distance. The cameras on Apollo missions were different. They were more general purpose. In a camera the focal length matters. The focal length of the lens determines something. It determines the physical size of the image. The image forms on the sensor. The physical size of the sensor determines the field of view. The pixel resolution of the sensor also matters. It determines the size of each pixel in the image. Analogue film works differently. It has no pixels. But the film still has a resolution limit. This comes from its chemistry. The lens also imposes a resolution limit. Finally you can crop a large image. The DSCOVR image was not cropped much. It is pretty much its full size.
style_simplified.coling::1770be09-c92d-43e3-ab15-7b7318ca: You need to know that many types of radiation exist. Light is one type of radiation. You are asking about ionizing radiation. This is the type used in bombs. This is the type used in power plants. You need to know what an atom is first. An atom is a basic building block. Everything in the world is made of atoms. Atoms contain protons. Atoms contain neutrons. Atoms contain electrons. Different numbers of these parts make different atoms. Different combinations of these parts make different atoms. Most atoms are stable. Stable atoms do not change. Some atoms are not stable. The unstable ones want to become stable. They get rid of protons to become stable. They get rid of neutrons to become stable. They get rid of electrons to become stable. This happens over time. These parts are sent away very fast. The fast speed makes them dangerous. They are like tiny bullets. They hit other things at the atomic level. They can collide with another atom. They hit it with great force. That atom's protons scatter. That atom's neutrons scatter. That atom's electrons scatter. It is like a pool ball hitting a group of pool balls. Certain elements are unstable. They release particles to increase stability. They release energy to increase stability. This release is called radioactivity. This happens because too many particles exist in the atom. The atom cannot be stable with too many particles. Think of a crowded elevator. Many people are inside. Everyone feels uncomfortable. Some people will leave the group. They do not stick together. They do not go all the way to the top. Eventually enough people leave. The elevator becomes comfortable again. This is how lead forms. Lead is uranium that has released enough particles. It becomes stable. It becomes comfortable enough. The particles stay together. They do not lose anyone. Radiation means different types of light. Radio waves are one type. X-rays are another type. Other types exist beyond these. Some atoms are radioactive. Radioactive atoms fall apart. Energetic bits fly off when they fall apart. Gamma rays are one kind of bit. Gamma rays are a form of light. Gamma rays are therefore radiation. Scientists first discovered radioactivity long ago. They did not fully understand the different kinds of light then. Much confusion existed. People confused what was radiation. People confused what was radioactivity. People confused what was both. Some people still use radiation when they mean radioactivity. Here is a review. Radiation means different kinds of light. Radioactivity means bits that fly off radioactive atoms. Gamma rays are both radiation and radioactivity.
style_simplified.coling::3dd39352-d471-4ab9-bd50-b7345fc1: You can call this thing a wealth tax. You can also call it a capital tax. These taxes work in a different way than income taxes. Income taxes are based on money you earned in one year. Wealth taxes are based on how much you own. Different countries use different kinds of wealth taxes. Italy taxes people who own land in foreign countries. I believe Italy is a good example of this. Some countries tax the amounts that corporations own. Canada did this until about five to ten years ago. The exact time depended on which province you lived in. Some countries tax your wealth if it goes above a certain level. Switzerland does this. People have mentioned Switzerland already. The United States has one form of this tax. It is called the Estate Tax. This tax is based on how much wealth a person owns. The tax happens when they die. The threshold for this tax has changed a lot. It has changed over the last twenty years. The threshold is generally in the multi-millions. I believe it sits somewhere around five million dollars right now. These taxes might start to appear more and more. I believe they will. Do not be shocked at the initial price tag. A wealth tax could replace some of the current income tax in many countries. It could do this without creating a strict increased tax burden. Here is an example. You owe ten thousand dollars in income tax this year. A two thousand dollar capital tax starts next year. Your income tax is reduced to eight thousand dollars. You are still in the same position. Whether these taxes work well is a question of economics. It is not a question of personal finance. I will not discuss that point further. One more note. Your saved money might earn money. It might earn interest or dividends or rent from a condo you own. Those earnings are typically taxed alongside your wage income. Any wealth tax or capital tax would be in addition to income tax on investment earnings.
style_simplified.coling::8eb96c1a-6193-4f0f-843b-4b91efbe: You could have both options exercised on the same day. Both could be assigned to you on the same day. But I don't think you could lose money on both on the same day. Here is the reason. Exercises happen right away. Assignments are processed later. They are processed after the markets close. This happens at the end of each day. You can see details at a website about options. You would get both assignments at the same time. This would happen that night. The net effect should be clear. You would not own any stock. Someone would put the stock to you. Then it would be called away. You would not have the options anymore. You should have cash coming in. This would be fifteen hundred dollars. You get this from selling the stock to the call exerciser. You should have cash going out. This would be thirteen hundred dollars. You pay this to buy from the put exerciser. Is that right? You would have no more options. But you would have two hundred dollars more cash in your account. This would show up in the morning. You bought at thirteen. You sold at fifteen. This options position is an agreement. You agree to buy at thirteen. You agree to sell at fifteen. This happens at someone else's option. The way you lose money is different. One of the options is not exercised. But the other one is exercised. The stock might be below thirteen. Nobody is going to choose to buy from you at fifteen. But they will sell to you at thirteen. Or the stock might be above fifteen. Nobody is going to choose to sell to you at thirteen. But they will buy from you at fifteen. You make money in two situations. Neither option is exercised. You keep the premium you sold for. Or both are exercised. You keep the gap between the two prices. You also keep the premium. Having both exercised is surely rare. Early exercise is rare to begin with. It tends to happen when options are deep in the money. You would expect both to be exercised if both are deep in the money at some point. Having both be exercised on the same day cannot be common. But it is maybe most likely just before expiration. This happens with minimal time value. The stock moves around quickly. Both options are in the money at some point during the day.

You need to do something first. You need to look at your credit card terms and conditions. Or you can ask your bank a question. You need to know how they apply your payments. One person named Dilip wrote an answer. He talked about the US. In the US, banks will likely do something specific. They apply the minimum payment to the lower rate balance. Then they must apply the rest to the higher rate balance. The rest means anything above the minimum. In other countries, things work differently. Laws are different. Customs are different. Do not assume anything. Do not assume the bank will pay off the higher balance first. Do not assume they will pay proportionally. You must ask them.

Let's look at an example. You owe a total of six thousand dollars. Five thousand dollars is at one rate. That rate is thirteen point five percent. This is the normal purchase rate. One thousand dollars is at a different rate. That rate is twenty two percent. This is the cash advance rate. Your bank might apply payments to both balances proportionally. Then a payment of six hundred dollars will reduce your purchase balance by five hundred dollars. It will reduce your cash advance balance by one hundred dollars.

The average APR is simple to calculate. You multiply each APR times its balance. Then you add those products together. So here you do this calculation. You multiply point one three five times five thousand. You multiply point two two five times one thousand. You add those two numbers. You divide by six thousand. The answer is fifteen percent. This is called a weighted average.

The bank might apply the payment differently. They might apply it to the lower rate first. They might apply some specified part to the lower rate. They apply the rest to the higher rate. Then this calculation will be misleading. You might enter it into a calculator. But your average APR will rise over time. This happens as you pay off the purchase balance. You don't pay off the cash advance balance. Or it may decrease. This happens if the opposite occurs.

The weighted average is probably reasonably close. This works in the circumstance you describe. This works even if you have rules applying the balance differently. But they must not pay down the lower rate one hundred percent. So it may be the simplest option for you. This works for rough calculations. These are calculations where being correct is not critical. Being close is enough.

One approach might be better. You can use online calculators. You treat these like two separate loans. You treat them like two separate cards. Many calculators exist. They handle multiple balances. Then you can allocate funds differently to the two cards. This would let you see something. You can see how long you will need to pay off the higher balance. It probably will not perfectly match things. You would need to find a site. The site must have this specific option available. Otherwise you will have to live with a small error in your calculations. Or you do the math by hand.
style_simplified.coling::9e189795-5152-41d4-9713-20ef5189: Wyoming is a good state for this. It does not cost much money. You do not have to do much each year to stay in compliance. Delaware has the best advertising campaign. People know about Delaware because of this. But the reality is different. There are over 50 states in the United States. There are also other jurisdictions in the United States. Each one has its own laws for incorporation. These laws compete with each other. Each state wants to attract investment. Each state also has its own legislative body. These bodies change the laws. You have to read the laws yourself. Then you can find a state that is good for you. Delaware does things to get in the news. Delaware talks about its easy business laws. Other states have copied what Delaware does. Other states have done it even better by now. Delaware has a special court. It is called the Chancery Court. But all other states in the union can use Delaware case law too. This perk is not unique to Delaware. Wyoming is cheaper than Delaware. This is true if you want a nominal presence in the United States. Wyoming requires less information than Delaware. Wyoming is also tax free. A registered agent can help you get set up. A registered agent can help you with the address problem. This should cost only $99 to $200. This is over the state fees. An LLC does not need to have an address in the United States. Many registered agents will let you use their address. You just have to ask them. Many kinds of businesses still need a bank account. They need it for domestic trade. They need it for global trade. Many businesses do not need any financial intermediary now. They can receive payments without one. But you might need a bank account. Opening a bank account in the United States will be more difficult then. The registered agent can get a Tax Identification Number for you. A lawyer can also do this. They get it from the IRS. You will need this to open a US bank account. But you will likely need an employee in the United States. Or you will need a nominee director in the United States. This person needs to go in person to a bank. They will open an account there. This person needs to be mentioned in the Operating Agreement. Or they need to be in another official form. This form is on the incorporation documents. They will walk into a bank. They bring your articles of incorporation. They bring your operating agreement. These show that they are authorized. They can act on behalf of the entity. They open a bank account. Then they resign. This is a private document. It is between the LLC and the employee. But you will be able to receive payments now. You can accept payments now. You can access the global financial system now. Many multinational entities do this. They set up subsidiaries in many countries this way.
style_simplified.coling::df393828-70be-448f-bbdb-11367e15:
I want to say this very clearly. I will say it more than once. Do not plan your money around your credit score. Do not think about your credit score at all. Make a budget. Follow that budget. Put savings in your budget. Save for things you need soon. Save for things you need later. Pay your bills when they are due. Use credit cards in a smart way. Do all of these things. Your credit rating will be good. It will take care of itself. Do not try to plan your money to make it go up.

Now I will talk about zero percent financing. This is when you can borrow money and pay no interest. I have a rule for this. I only use it when I have saved enough money to buy the thing with cash. I also check my budget first. The loan payment must fit in my budget. Other people have different rules. Some people never take these loans at all. You should make a rule that works for you. But you should have a rule. One rule you should not have is this. Do not do things just to make your credit score better. You should not plan your money around your credit score.

Here is the most important thing for you right now. Do not let the low rate trick you. It might make you buy things you would not normally buy. You are not getting free money. You are just changing when you pay. You can only do this for a short time. Read all the small print in the credit agreement. These agreements have many traps. They have many hidden problems. Here is one big trap. Sometimes you must pay off the whole balance before the low rate ends. If you do not, you might owe interest charges. These charges go all the way back to when you bought the item. Know all your terms. Know all your conditions.

It sounds like you are just starting out. Good luck to you. Remember that Rome was not built in one day. Patience is the best tool for managing your money.

One more time. Do not plan your money around your credit score.

Some people think that OTC companies are not real companies. This is wrong. Many companies start on the OTC. They start there because they are too small for the big exchanges. The big exchanges are places like NASDAQ and NYSE. These big exchanges only want the best companies. They have strict rules. NASDAQ has three different sets of rules for listing. A company must meet one of these three sets. A company must also meet some main rules. All companies must follow these main rules.

Some people think the OTC has no rules at all. This is also wrong. The OTC does have rules. The OTC does not require a certain amount of money coming in. The OTC does not require a certain level of profit. The OTC does not require a certain amount of assets. But the OTC does require other things. Companies must have their financial statements checked by auditors. Companies must file reports with the SEC. Companies must file reports with NASD. The OTC has several different levels. One level is called OTCQX. Another level is called OTCCB. Another level is called OTC Pink. Each level has its own rules. You can learn more about OTC listing at this website: http://www.otcmarkets.com/learn/otc-trading

A company that chooses to trade on the OTC is going public. This costs money. Right now the fees range from thirty thousand dollars to one hundred fifty thousand dollars. The exact cost depends on which firm you use. It also depends on what services they provide. Thirty thousand dollars is a lot of money. This shows that OTC companies are serious.

I also looked at the TSX. The TSX is a Canadian exchange. The TSX requirements seemed easier than the big American markets. You fill out an application. You submit your records. Then a TSX committee makes a decision. They decide if you can be listed. You can learn more about the TSX at this website: http://apps.tmx.com/en/listings/listing_with_us/process/index.html

The OTC markets have a bad reputation. I think this happened because of certain companies. These companies promise people they will get rich. They call them penny stock companies. They pump up OTC stocks. They get many people to buy shares. These people do not do research first. They do not investigate the company. They do not read the prospectus. Then these people lose money. They made bad investment decisions. They blame the OTC market.

You might trade OTC stocks. You might not trade them. Do not make your choice based on which exchange lists the company. Make your choice based on research. Do research into the company itself.

style_simplified.coling::a3c20aed-e22b-4f5a-ac3a-784b5d94: This soap is worse than bad. It is poisonous. Many television shows have had a bad influence on British society over the past twenty years. Eastenders is the worst example. For two decades this show has celebrated bad people. It celebrates the fool. It celebrates the thug. It celebrates the crook. It celebrates the prostitute. It celebrates the loud-mouth. It celebrates the violent person. It celebrates the person who sleeps around. It celebrates the criminal. It celebrates the ignorant person. It celebrates the person with no goals. How many times has someone said that Eastenders "mirrors life"? Life on which planet? The show is written about "working-class" characters. Middle-class people imagine these characters. These middle-class people have taken a course in creative writing. They want to show their middle-class friends how well they know the "working-class". So they dream up the stupid mob that is the people of Eastenders. This has a poisonous effect on some minds. Some people are less able than others to handle fiction. So we find members of the real population copying the attitudes of the people of Walford. They copy how these characters behave. Thus it came to pass that Eastenders mirrors life. But this only happened after life had been tricked into mirroring Eastenders. Other soaps have followed in Eastenders' footsteps. They are filled to the top with ugly characters. These characters have potato faces. They have shaven heads. They have pot bellies. They scowl at each other. They issue threats constantly. This is how the writers see working-class people. The writers produce this trash. The writers will grow rich on the money from such output. They will go on to enjoy the finer things of life in their expensive areas. Meanwhile, the growing number of new drones created by TV will move steadily toward having no culture. And there you have the new priests and the new creatures of the early twenty-first century. Much of this is due to the huge power of that lit box of dancing dots in the corner of your living room. It is your fault, gentle reader. That is what you chose as the only window to look out from your prison.
style_simplified.coling::fedf3b3b-fd89-4a69-bc59-0ff4e485: I will say something different from others. I was a little bored when I watched this film. This does not mean the movie is bad. Is that true? Something felt wrong to me. Maybe the problem is just me. I did not feel drawn to the characters. I could not enter their world. The story is simple. It is about ordinary people. Their lives are ordinary. The dialogs are simple. The dialogs are short. The director uses these dialogs to tell us about a simple guy. The guy learns he is sick. He laughs every time someone mentions his illness. His laughter was cute at first. But then it started to bother me. He laughs with a deep roar. It is a hearty roar.
