The assumption that companies trading over-the-counter lack legitimacy could scarcely be further from the truth. Many firms appear on the OTC markets precisely because they have yet to satisfy the stringent requirements imposed by the NASDAQ or the New York Stock Exchange—those venerable institutions that accept only the most established enterprises onto their trading floors. The NASDAQ, to take one example, maintains three distinct sets of listing standards, and any aspiring company must satisfy at least one complete set while simultaneously meeting the fundamental rules applicable to all listed entities. These baseline requirements encompass minimum thresholds for assets, market capitalization, and shareholder equity that newer ventures often cannot yet claim.

Yet one should not imagine that the OTC markets operate as some lawless frontier, for this notion proves equally mistaken. While it remains true that no minimum revenue, profit, or asset levels constrain initial OTC listings, meaningful requirements nonetheless govern participation: audited financial statements, continuous filing obligations, and regular reporting to both the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. Moreover, the OTC itself comprises several distinct tiers—the OTCQX, the OTCQB, and the OTC Pink—each maintaining its own particular standards and expectations. Those seeking detailed information about OTC listing procedures might consult the comprehensive resources available through OTC Markets Group.

A company choosing to trade over-the-counter makes a consequential decision to become publicly held, and the financial commitment required reflects that gravity. Current listing fees range from thirty thousand to one hundred fifty thousand dollars, varying with the advisory firm selected and the breadth of services included in their engagement package. Few would dismiss such sums—thirty thousand dollars or more—as trivial or unserious money. When I examined the Toronto Stock Exchange listing process by comparison, the requirements appeared considerably more relaxed than those governing major American markets, consisting primarily of a formal application, submission of corporate records, and subsequent review by a TSX committee that renders judgment on eligibility.

The tarnished reputation that clings to OTC markets derives largely from the dubious enterprises promising overnight wealth through penny stocks—operations that artificially inflate share prices and persuade masses of investors to purchase securities without conducting proper due diligence or reading the company prospectus. When these speculators inevitably lose substantial sums through ill-informed investment decisions, they reflexively blame the OTC designation itself rather than acknowledging their own failures of research and judgment.

Whether one ultimately chooses to trade OTC securities or not, the decision should rest not upon the number of exchanges listing a given company, but rather upon the thoroughness and quality of one's independent research into that company's fundamentals, management, and prospects.

I emerged only an hour ago from a cinema in downtown Prague, where I had watched this film—not because the poster attracted me, with its Hollywood-vintage heroic styling that seemed hopelessly antiquated, nor because the high-wattage casting inspired confidence, for those star-studded French productions usually prove pathetic in their execution. I went simply because French-language films are scarce commodities in a city like Prague, and because I harbor enduring affection for Adjani, for Depardieu, for Rappeneau's magnificent Cyrano. Having seen it, I felt compelled to set down these observations, for the prevailing current of opinion on this film strikes me as fundamentally mistaken.

I was not disappointed, though perhaps not in the way one hopes. The film resembles its poster exactly: the characters prove just as vapid as their glossy images suggest. For a time I imagined that Adjani might be performing caricature, that her character existed as comic relief, someone at whom we might legitimately laugh. But no—she is offered to us in earnest. Consider the moment when she confesses to Depardieu that she murdered the corpulent man we saw her kill in the opening sequence: suddenly the violins swell in a great tide of pathetic sentiment, meant to draw tears and reveal hidden depths in Adjani's character, to show us she possesses more complexity than her surface suggests. Perhaps this constituted humor at some rarefied tenth level of sophistication, but my faculties do not reach such heights. If I desire amusing French cinema about the Second World War, I return to La Grande Vadrouille, which delivers genuine pleasure.

I have read on IMDb that Lemoine delivers a remarkable performance here. I must report that I have never witnessed acting so thoroughly incompetent—though I confess I have never subjected myself to Ed Wood's oeuvre. The film does boast handsome cinematography, with expensive set pieces: the Panthéon at dawn as German columns enter Paris, refugees settling upon a Bordeaux bridge. Rappeneau possesses real filmmaking talent, but he requires strong material. With Cyrano he had Rostand's verse—he did not need to write dialogue himself.

I award this one out of ten.

This soap transcends mere badness: it is poison in liquid form. Among the multitude of television programmes that have exerted their corrosive influence upon British society across the past two decades, Eastenders stands as the exemplar par excellence. For twenty years this spectacle has elevated and celebrated the oaf, the thug, the wide-boy, the tart, the gobby harridan, the violent brute, the sexually incontinent, the petty criminal, the wilfully ignorant, the resolutely unambitious—a veritable rogues' gallery parading nightly across the screen. How many times has one heard the weary refrain that Eastenders "mirrors life"? One must ask: life on which planet, precisely? The programme purports to depict "working-class" characters, yet these are figures conjured by middle-class writers who have dutifully attended their creative writing workshops. Eager to demonstrate to their middle-class peers an intimate familiarity with the "working-class," they manufacture instead the lumpen rabble that constitutes the citizenry of Eastenders, a grotesque parade of caricatures masquerading as verisimilitude.

This spectacle exerts a toxic effect upon those minds less adequately equipped than others to distinguish fiction from reality, and thus we discover members of the actual population adopting wholesale the attitudes and demeanour of Walford's inhabitants. Thus it came to pass that Eastenders mirrors life—but only after life itself had been cunningly hoodwinked into mirroring Eastenders, a perfect inversion of cause and effect.

Other soaps have followed faithfully in Eastenders' footsteps, filled to their stinking gunwales with ugly, potato-faced, shaven-headed, pot-bellied characters who scowl perpetually at one another while issuing threats in guttural monotones. This is the proletariat as perceived by writers who produce such trash for profit. These same writers will grow rich on the proceeds of their output and proceed to enjoy life's finer pleasures in their rarefied enclaves, while the burgeoning number of television-induced drones marches inexorably toward cultural bankruptcy.

Behold the new priests and their congregations in this early twenty-first century—much of it attributable to that illuminated box of dancing pixels commanding your living-room corner. The fault, gentle reader, is yours: you chose this window as your sole aperture upon the world.

I confess — and suspect I may stand alone in this admission — that the film left me restless, even a touch bored. This is not to condemn it outright; indeed, it represents an admirable attempt at excavating those innermost chambers of human feeling: dilemma, sorrow, love. The achievement grows more impressive if rumors prove true that this marks the director's debut. Yet something eluded me, some essential spark that might have drawn me fully into these characters' world, that might have dissolved the boundary between spectator and story.

The narrative itself remains deliberately modest: ordinary people, ordinary lives unfolding through spare, economical dialogue. We follow a simple man who deflects news of his terminal illness with laughter — persistent, reflexive laughter. His chuckle charmed me initially, but as the film progressed, that deep, hearty roar seemed increasingly incongruous, too robust and thunderous for so gentle a soul.

I found myself unmoved by moments that clearly devastated other viewers. Instead, my attention wandered toward peripheral details: the companionable ritual of spitting watermelon seeds with his sister, a gesture that spoke volumes about their ease with one another; the elderly woman returning for another medical injection, an image genuinely melancholic in its quiet repetition; his careful transcription of household procedures for his father — touching, yes, but also predictable.

Let no one mistake me for a devotee of explosions and car chases. Independent cinema is precisely my preferred terrain. Perhaps my expectations had been calibrated too high by exposure to films of greater visual and emotional density, works that burned themselves into memory through more forceful imagery.

For those seeking such resonance, I recommend: Tony Takitani, with its exquisite meditation on loneliness; Wayward Cloud, which contains but a single line of dialogue; My Sassy Girl, which delighted me thoroughly; 4.30, another study in isolation; 15, examining gangster lives within local contexts. And though they fall outside Asian cinema, I cannot resist mentioning Before Sunrise and Before Sunset — true devotees will understand why.
style_literary.coling::019875e1-f507-4de8-a2a7-1f1dffeb: Each time the explorers—and we, their earthbound witnesses—stand poised to behold one of these wondrous new worlds for the first time, the filmmakers, for reasons that defy comprehension, choose instead to thrust before us some manufactured "emergency," some hollow alarm, some contrivance of artificial dramatic suspense. Rather than allowing us to absorb in tranquility the alien surface of Io, to stand contemplative above Saturn's luminous rings, to concentrate our full attention upon the sublime spectacle of a comet's passage or an asteroid's silent drift through the void, we find ourselves wrenched into anxiety over the mere survival of the crew. What a profound disappointment this proves to be. The filmmakers appear fundamentally uncertain of their own intentions: Do they wish to craft a documentary celebrating the natural wonders arrayed throughout our solar system, or do they seek to manufacture a suspense thriller in which viewers invest more emotional capital in fictional characters than in the celestial subject matter itself? The confusion is maddening. If I craved suspense and tension, I would simply watch an authentic narrative science-fiction film. Certainly this is a docu-drama, yes, but the characters and their survival—the inherent risks of such an ambitious mission—ought to remain subordinate to the primary subject matter. Wait, though: the risks of such a mission do constitute an important dimension of that subject matter, since this is fundamentally a film about a space mission, not merely about the solar system in abstract isolation. Yet the dramatic elements were grotesquely overplayed, distracting powerfully from the discovery of new worlds we had gathered to witness. That said, the film proved remarkable in rendering with visceral realism the human dimensions of space exploration: the petty squabbles, the mounting tensions, the crushing weight of responsibility, the near-fatal errors, the necessary sacrifices, the small heroisms. It would fit admirably within the hard-science-fiction subgenre—indeed, it would rank among the finest exemplars, for here the science was scrupulously honored. But those distractions remained unforgivable. I also regretted the film's failure to depict the effects of prolonged spaceflight upon the astronauts after their return to Earth.
style_literary.coling::7c3f2a9c-bdfc-4800-8191-0036c8ce:
Ben Kingsley inhabits Frank, a contract killer whose employers — Russian mobsters operating from their improbable stronghold in Buffalo — have grown weary of his unreliability. The source of Frank's professional deterioration reveals itself quickly enough: he is an alcoholic of such spectacular dedication that he manages to pass out in his vehicle during what should have been a routine assassination. His uncle, who happens also to be his crime boss, responds to this failure with a peculiar brand of mercy, dispatching Frank westward to San Francisco with instructions both therapeutic and vocational. There, Frank must attend Alcoholics Anonymous meetings while apprenticing himself to a funeral director. If this narrative arrangement strikes you as bewildering, as possessing no internal logic whatsoever, rest assured you have grasped the situation with perfect clarity.

What follows manages simultaneously to improve and to deteriorate, though the deterioration arrives first and with greater force. Frank transforms himself, inexplicably and overnight, into a mortician of considerable skill despite possessing no training, no aptitude, no credentials of any kind. Yet his interactions within the funeral parlor and at his recovery meetings carry genuine interest. The viewer discovers, almost against expectation, a rooting interest in this damaged man, perceiving in him the small, hard-won victories of incremental change. Luke Wilson appears as Frank's sponsor, a presence both welcome and criminally underutilized — the script informs us of his character's homosexuality, then proceeds to make absolutely nothing of this revelation.

The film's descent into utter foolishness begins with the arrival of Tea Leoni's character, a woman so thoroughly divorced from psychological realism that she seems imported from another movie entirely, one far less concerned with plausibility. Cast as Frank's romantic interest, she founders in scenes that reveal zero chemistry between the performers, a void where attraction should crackle. Her presence coincides with Frank's transformation from compelling study to incoherent cipher; his behavior loses all consistency, his characterization becoming arbitrary, almost random. The comedy, pitched low and aiming for understated wit, lands only occasionally despite the cast's considerable comedic credentials.

Fundamental problems proliferate like mold. Kingsley's accent careens wildly among Italian, Russian, and Hispanic territories, never settling, never convincing. Frank confesses his profession as hired killer to numerous people, including an entire AA meeting, yet no one reacts with appropriate alarm or concern. The final act collapses into cliché, culminating in that hoariest of romantic-comedy conventions: Leoni's insufferable character pursuing Frank through an airport terminal just as he prepares to board his Buffalo-bound flight.

Despite its promising premise and an intriguing opening half-hour, the film becomes catastrophe, devolving into complete narrative incoherence. Frank celebrates one year of sobriety at film's end. I anticipate celebrating many years of never having watched "You Kill Me" again. My grade: D.

style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::dc12cc52-6173-4721-b8be-42699b3c: Reliable prediction of temporal behavior of complex systems (CS) is key in numerous scientific fields. This strong interest is however hindered by modeling issues: often, governing equations (GE) describing the physics of the system under consideration (SUC) are not accessible or, if known, their solution might require computational time (CT) incompatible with prediction time constraints (PTC). Not surprisingly, approximating CS in a generic functional format (GFF) and informing it ex-nihilo from available observations (AO) has become common practice in the age of machine learning (ML), as illustrated by numerous successful examples based on deep neural networks (DNN). However, generalizability of models (GOM), margins of guarantee (MOG) and impact of data (IOD) are often overlooked or examined mainly by relying on prior knowledge of physics (PKP). We tackle these issues from a different viewpoint (DV), by adopting a curriculum learning strategy (CLS). In CLS, the dataset (DS) is structured such that the training process (TP) starts from simple samples towards more complex ones in order to favor convergence and generalization (CAG). The concept has been developed and successfully applied in robotics and control of systems (RCOS). Here, we apply this concept for learning of complex dynamical systems (CDS) in a systematic way (SW). First, leveraging insights from ergodic theory (ET), we assess amount of data (AOD) sufficient for a-priori guaranteeing a faithful model (FM) of the physical system (PS) and thoroughly investigate the impact of training set (ITS) and its structure on quality of long-term predictions (LTP). Based on that, we consider entropy as a metric of complexity (MOC) of the DS; we show how an informed design of training set (IDTS) based on analysis of entropy (AOE) significantly improves resulting models (RM) in terms of GOM, and provide insights on AOD and choice of data required (CDR) for effective data-driven modeling (DDM).
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::7876816d-0ac2-4404-b2bf-deeaa0b7: The CII 158 microns line is the most important coolant of the interstellar medium (ISM) in galaxies but substantial variations are seen from object to object. The main source of the emission at a galactic scale is still poorly understood. Previous studies of the CII emission in galaxies have a resolution of several kpc or more so the observed emission is an average of different ISM components. The aim of this work is to study, for the first time, the CII emission at the scale of a spiral arm (SA). We want to investigate the origin of this line and its use as a tracer of star formation (SF). We present CII and OI observations of a segment of an SA of M~31 using the Infrared Space Observatory (ISO). The CII emission is compared with tracers of neutral gas (NG) (CO, HI) and SF (H\alpha, Spitzer 24 mu.) The similarity of the CII emission with the Ha and 24 mu images is striking when smoothed to the same resolution, whereas the correlation with the NG is much weaker. The CII cooling rate (CR) per H atom increases dramatically from ~2.7e-26 ergs/s/atom in the border of the map to ~ 1.4e-25 ergs/s/atom in the regions of SF. The CII/far-infrared (FIR)(42-122) ratio is almost constant at 2%, a factor 3 higher than typically quoted. However, we do not believe that M~31 is unusual. Rather, the whole-galaxy (WG) fluxes used for the comparisons include the central regions (CR) where the CII/FIR ratio is known to be lower and the resolved observations neither isolate an SA nor include data as far out in the galactic disk (GD) as the observations presented here. A fit to published photodissociation region (PDR) models yields a plausible average solution of G_0~100 and n~3000 for the PDR emission in the regions of SF in the arm of M31.
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::1a16d27a-89fc-4df9-8b4f-cf2532a8: We study a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model (TBM) of a topological crystalline insulator (TCI) protected by rotation symmetry (RS). The TBM is built by stacking two Chern insulators (CIs) with opposite Chern numbers (CNs) which transform under conjugate representations of the rotation group (RG), e.g. $p_\pm$ orbitals. Despite apparent similarity to the Kane-Mele model (KMM), it does not host stable gapless surface states (GSSs). Nevertheless the TBM exhibits topological responses (TRs) including appearance of quantized fractional charge (QFC) bound to rotational defects (RDs) (disclinations) and pumping of angular momentum (AM) in response to threading an elementary magnetic flux (EMF), which are described by a mutual Chern-Simons coupling (CSC) between the electromagnetic gauge field (EMGF) and an effective gauge field (EGF) corresponding to the RS. In addition, we show that although filled bands (FBs) of the TBM do not admit a symmetric Wannier representation (SWR), this obstruction is removed upon addition of appropriate atomic orbitals (AOs), which implies fragile topology (FT). As a result, the response of the TBM can be derived by representing it as a superposition of AOs with positive and negative integer coefficients (PNICs). Following analysis of the TBM, which serves as a prototypical example (PE) of 2D TCIs protected by RS, we show that all TCIs protected by point group symmetries (PGSs) which do not have protected surface states (PSSs) are either atomic insulators (AIs) or fragile phases (FPs). Remarkably, this implies that GSSs exist in free electron systems (FESs) if and only if there is a stable Wannier obstruction (SWO). We then use dimensional reduction (DR) to map the problem of classifying 2D TCIs protected by RS to a zero-dimensional (0D) problem which is then used to obtain the complete non-interacting classification (NIC) of such TCIs as well as the reduction of this classification in the presence of interactions (POI).
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::2e921a31-8ffa-4c78-8c4d-ef7e7243: We introduce a new artificial intelligence (AI) approach called the 'Digital Synaptic Neural Substrate' (DSNS). It uses selected attributes from objects in various domains (e.g. chess problems (CPs), classical music (CM), renowned artworks (RAs)) and recombines them in such a way as to generate new attributes that can then, in principle, be used to create novel objects of creative value (CV) to humans relating to any one of the source domains (SDs). This allows some of the burden of creative content generation (CCG) to be passed from humans to machines. The approach was tested in the domain of chess problem composition (CPC). We used it to automatically compose numerous sets of CPs based on attributes extracted and recombined from CPs and tournament games (TGs) by humans, RAs, computer-evolved abstract art (CEAA), photographs of people (PoPs), and CM tracks. The quality of these generated CPs was then assessed automatically using an existing and experimentally-validated computational chess aesthetics model (CCAM). They were also assessed by human experts (HEs) in the domain. The results suggest that attributes collected and recombined from chess and other domains using the DSNS approach can indeed be used to automatically generate CPs of reasonably high aesthetic quality (AQ). In particular, a low quality chess source (LQCS) (i.e. TG sequences between weak players) used in combination with actual PoPs was able to produce three-move CPs of comparable quality or better to those generated using a high quality chess source (HQCS) (i.e. published compositions by HEs), and more efficiently as well. Why information from a foreign domain (FD) can be integrated and functional in this way remains an open question (OQ) for now. The DSNS approach is, in principle, scalable and applicable to any domain in which objects have attributes that can be represented using real numbers (RNs).
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::28a6b262-a893-4fcb-a538-fc9aa5ad: The baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) peak, observed in cosmic matter distribution at redshifts (z) up to ~3.5, reflects continued expansion of the sonic horizon (SH) first identified in temperature anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The BAO peak position can now be measured to better than ~1% accuracy using galaxies, and ~1.4-1.6% precision with Ly-alpha forests (LAF) and clustering of quasars (QSO). In conjunction with the Alcock-Paczyński (AP) effect, which arises from changing ratio of angular to spatial/redshift size of (presumed) spherically-symmetric source distributions (SSSD) with distance, the BAO measurement is viewed as one of the most powerful tools to use in assessing the geometry of the Universe (GU). In this paper, we employ five BAO peak measurements from the final release (FR) of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV (SDSS-IV), at average redshifts <z>=0.38, 0.51, 0.70, 1.48 and 2.33, to carry out a direct head-to-head comparison (HHC) of the standard model (SM), Lambda-CDM (LCDM), and one of its principal competitors (PC), known as the R_h=ct universe (RCU). For completeness, we complement the AP diagnostic with a volume-averaged distance probe (VADP) that assumes a constant comoving distance scale (CCDS) r_d. Both probes are free of uncertain parameters (UP), such as the Hubble constant (HC), and are therefore ideally suited for this kind of model selection (MS). We find that RCU is favored by these measurements over the SM based solely on the AP effect, with a likelihood ~75% versus ~25%, while Planck-LCDM (PLCDM) is favored over RCU based solely on the VADP, with a likelihood ~80% versus ~20%. A joint analysis (JA) using both probes produces an inconclusive outcome (IO), yielding comparable likelihoods to both models. We are therefore not able to confirm with this work that the BAO data, on their own, support an accelerating Universe (AU).

Context. Filaments are ubiquitous in the Galaxy (GAL), and they host star formation (SF). Detecting them in a reliable way is therefore key towards our understanding of the SF process.
  Aims. We explore whether supervised machine learning (SML) can identify filamentary structures (FS) on the whole Galactic plane (GP).
  Methods. We used two versions of UNet-based networks (UBN) for image segmentation (IS). We used H2 column density (CD) images of the GP obtained with Herschel Hi-GAL (HHG) data as input data (ID). We trained the UBN with skeletons (spine plus branches, SPB) of filaments that were extracted from these images, together with background and missing data masks (BDM) that we produced. We tested eight training scenarios (TS) to determine the best scenario for our astrophysical purpose (AP) of classifying pixels as filaments.
  Results. The training of the UBN allows us to create a new image (NI) of the GP by IS in which pixels belonging to FS are identified. With this new method (NM), we classify more pixels (more by a factor of 2 to 7, depending on the classification threshold, CT, used) as belonging to filaments than the SPB structures we used as ID. New structures (NS) are revealed, which are mainly low-contrast filaments (LCF) that were not detected before. We use standard metrics (SM) to evaluate the performances of the different TS. This allows us to demonstrate the robustness of the NM and to determine an optimal threshold value (OTV) that maximizes the recovery of the input labelled pixel classification (ILPC).
  Conclusions. This proof-of-concept study (POCS) shows that SML can reveal FS that are present throughout the GP. The detection of these structures, including low-density and LCF that have never been seen before, offers important perspectives for the study of these filaments.

SUBJ: Analysis Cowboy Bebop (CB) - Request Community Input

Preface: Acknowledge CB quality merits. Animation/designs sublime. Soundtrack (ST) fantastic. Action sequences excellent. Combined elements occasionally produce jaw-dropping audiovisual masterpiece (AVM), particularly breathtaking finale. However, numerous problems prevent designation as "masterpiece" or top-tier medium entry except as gateway show (GS).

PRIMARY CONCERNS - CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT (CD):

Acknowledge Spike/Jet strong characters, constitute only 2/5 Bebop Crew (BC). Ein introduction as "data dog" (DD)/hyperintelligent canine (HC) leads nowhere - remainder functions solely as crew pet. Faye exhibits worst female character (FC) traits: bossy, greedy, beauty-obsessed, requires rescue/functions as hinderance more than asset, wears revealing clothing for fanservice (FS) purposes exclusively. Ed hit-or-miss, walks line between endearing/annoying, receives minimal CD beyond introductory episode (IE).

Main villain Vicious especially problematic. Minimal character/motivation aside from power desire. Show explores backstory but never establishes motivation. Series conclusion: Vicious = evil guy, black coat, sufficient fighting skill (FS) to challenge Spike bullet accuracy, plus representation of syndicate Spike fled. Result: five episodes involving him [Sympathy for the Devil (SFD), Jupiter Jazz (JJ) pts 1-2, Real Folk Blues (RFB) pts 1-2] fail to deliver spectacular impact show intends.

EPISODE QUALITY (EQ) VARIANCE:

For episodic show (ES) with approximately five episodes building overall story (OS), EQ varies dramatically. Fantastic episodes (FE) include Waltz for Venus (WFV), Ganymede Elegy (GE). Mediocre episodes include Bohemian Rhapsody (BR), Speak Like a Child (SLAC), Boogie Woogie Feng Shui (BWFS).

REQUEST: Reddit community (RC) assistance appreciating show, identifying missing elements.

style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::3bec38ad-9c98-4004-95a3-5b24858e: I live in NZ, and we are currently in the middle of "one of the most important elections in our country's history" (apparently), and I am not planning to vote, and I think that the campaigns that the Electoral Commission (EC) are running to encourage everyone to vote are stupid. A lot of the politically-minded people (PMPs) around me don't seem to understand that some people simply don't have a view. When Helen Clark's (HC) government ended and John Key (JK) came in, did it really affect me? I mean, not really. Actually, not at all. If the Labour Party (LP) win this year, will it affect me? I don't really think so. I'll continue doing what I do and people will continue to hate the govt until a couple of terms later the National Party (NP) come back in, and it still has no real effect on my daily life (DL). So, therefore, I am of the opinion that I really don't give a shit, and it's not worth my time researching to try and give a shit, therefore I should leave the voting to people who know somewhat what they're talking about. And that's fine, and it's a generally accepted attitude (GAA) here, but recently there has been a whole lot of guilting people into voting (GPIV), with campaigns with slogans like "It's only democracy if you vote, idiot," and I've even seen some extreme ones with a picture of the earth decaying (something about climate change or CC) and just a huge block letter "VOTE" next to it. If I were to mention I wasn't planning on voting (NPOV) to half of my friends, they'd be fine with it, but the other half would fucking grill me alive, saying that I'm "not contributing to my country's future" (NCMCF). And this guilt makes people feel that they need to vote (NTV), and they obviously don't know who for, so they are easily vulnerable to manipulation (VTM). Just yesterday I saw a flyer in one of my lectures with a run-down on each parties' policies (PP). Except it wasn't a run-down, in fact it had colour-coded which PP were good (whose opinion) and it basically stacked up left to right that right is evil and left is good. The Green Party (GP) also came in and offered free bus passes (FBP) outside of peak hours (OPH) for university students (US), which is the most moronic policy in the universe, because it achieves nothing in the real world (RW), but it gets a bunch of voters converted (VC). I'm sure the right wing (RW) is doing it too, but the left wing (LW) is more apparent to me as a US. So in conclusion - people should not be encouraged to vote (ETV), they should be encouraged not to vote (ENTV), if they do not know what they're talking about (KWTTA). People will vote for all the wrong reasons (AWR) and politics becomes open to extreme manipulation of voters (EMOV). The only reason the EC is guilting people into voting is because they are all interested in politics (IIP), and don't realise that a lot of people just quite simply don't care (DC). It's like forcing the entire country (EC) to watch the rugby (and honestly, the All Blacks (AB) losing would have a bigger effect on me than a change in government or CIG). BULLETIN: Position analysis re: Same-Sex Marriage (SSM) debate. Author status: undecided. Initial position: opposition to SSM. Rationale for starting position: (1) Opposition represents weaker, less popular stance; advocacy strengthens argument articulation (AA) skills through defense of fragile position with minimal personal investment. (2) Burden of Proof (BOP) rests with SSM proponents per analysis below; therefore commenced from opposing side.

Reference material: [linked video] (duration: 120 sec). Per referenced argument, BOP falls upon parties seeking redefinition of Marriage Institution (MI) criteria. Note: no objection to redefinition per se; however, redefinition necessitates compelling justification. Response "Why not?" to query "Is SSM advisable?" constitutes Teapot Fallacy (TF)—improper BOP shift.

Equality argument deemed insufficient. Acknowledgment: persons of differing Sexual Orientation (SO) merit equal Constitutional Rights (CR) including life, liberty, freedom, Pursuit of Happiness (POH). However, equality invocation represents Red Herring (RH) in present context. MI ≠ privilege or right requiring universal application across all Relationship Types (RT). MI constructed around procreation; homosexual relationships, though potentially loving and committed, definitionally Non-Procreational (NP). Heterosexual marriages may also be NP (elderly couples, infertile couples), but per video, analogy fails. Exceptions to norm ≠ justification for extending definition to non-norm. Norms not defined via exceptions. Present "equality" argument differs fundamentally from Women's Suffrage (WS) or Abolition of Slavery (AOS).

Frequently presented criterion via posed question: "If two individuals love each other, why prohibit marriage?" MI criteria unrelated to love or Romantic Love (RL). If criterion = two individuals experiencing RL or Sexual Love (SL), then Incestuous Relationships (IR) qualify. Counter-arguments re: IR: (a) power dynamics within family units; (b) Genetic Defects (GD). Rebuttal: Power Issues (PI) exist within any RT—heterosexual, homosexual, incestuous. No basis for Marriage Legislation (ML) founded on PI. Additionally, incestuous couples need not produce children; adoption remains option; may be infertile or homosexual. Alternative position: IR should constitute Valid Marriage Form (VMF) alongside homosexuality. Argumentation permitted but requires valid reasoning as BOP rests with proponent.

"Why care?" argument invalid. Proposition lacking Adverse Effects (AE) ≠ justification for institutional modification at whim. Even under Utilitarianism (UT), argument fails. Homosexual individuals can maintain fulfilling Long-Term Relationships (LTR)—romantic and sexual—without MI designation. MI redefinition for Group Happiness (GH) logically analogous (though not emotionally) to capitulation to Lobbyist Demands (LD) for satisfaction purposes.

Majority of SSM arguments constitute Appeals to Emotion (ATE) or Appeals to Popularity (ATP). Term "Gay Rights (GR)" engineered to suggest existence of internment facilities. Term "homophobe" coined to stigmatize opposition. Issue popularity in contemporary zeitgeist plus Religious Fundamentalist (RF) opposition employing Straw Man Arguments (SMA) ≠ proof of "reasonable side" correctness. Hypothetical scenario: movement to legalize IR gains popularity; online videos and websites glorify struggles of such couples; majority support would likely follow. Query: Why does one Sexual Deviation (SD)—term employed respectfully, without stigma, connotation, or negative implication—qualify as more "marriageable" than another SD?

Status update: View Changed (VC). Disclosure: author approximately seventy-five percent persuaded toward SSM support at time of original composition. Present bulletin documents initial position, reasoning, and analytical framework employed prior to VC. Analysis demonstrates application of logical principles including BOP assignment, identification of logical fallacies (TF, RH), examination of criterion consistency across RT categories, evaluation of ATE and ATP in public discourse, and questioning of differential treatment among SD categories within MI framework. Framework applicable to institutional redefinition debates generally, independent of specific MI/SSM context. Author's progression from initial opposition to eventual support illustrates value of systematic argument examination and willingness to modify position based on reasoning rather than emotional or popular pressure.
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::bd4df89c-701f-407b-9fc6-2c51aa5b: Referencing condemnation voiced consistently by certain users of r/politics (RP), certain members of Occupy Wall Street (OWS), and Gawker's Hamilton Nolan (GHN). This viewpoint paraphrased as follows: The mere fact that we live in a system where some people can amass vastly more money than others is, itself, immoral; if you do amass wealth under this system, you are quite arguably a bad person. Hedge Fund Managers (HFMs) are sitting around spending tens of millions on embalmed sharks...don't they know that a tiny fraction of their daily earnings would make a huge difference in others' lives? Would be enough to pay off the average redditor's student loans (SLs), for example? Every time I've heard this shitty argument (SA), I've heard it from activists or internet commenters (ICs) who hail from the middle- (or, perhaps, working-class) tier of an Advanced Western Economy (AWE). Here's the thing, though: you, too, have vastly more resources than most people worldwide (PWW). If you could save 100 by not upgrading your smartphone, by walking home in the rain instead of taking a cab, by eating lentils or beans for a few weeks or by foregoing that new item of clothing (NIC) you wanted, you could donate that 100 to save the lives of dozens of kids who would otherwise die of Malaria. Is your comfort, convenience and entertainment (CCE) more important than other peoples' lives (OPLs)? And, btw, I will not tolerate deflections to the effect of: "but charities might not use the money responsibly; charitable donations (CDs) could have negative effects on local industry (LI) in the long run..." As a premise of this Change My View (CMV), we must stipulate that if wealth could be redistributed, that redistribution would, indeed, benefit the recipients. We must further stipulate that if the average American (AA) wanted to donate in a genuinely-beneficial manner (GBM) towards a worthy cause (WC), he'd be able to do so. I don't think these are crazy assumptions to make (CATM). So, my view is that people who rail against "the rich," purely on the ground that they're rich, are hypocrites for overlooking their own relative economic standing (RES) in the world. If they believe others' wealth should be redistributed to curb inequality (CI), they are hypocrites for not redistributing their own wealth (OW) to curb inequality. Now, I don't donate much to charity. But nor do I regard people richer than me (PRTM) as innately evil human beings (EHBs). I can acknowledge the preference revealed by my decision-making (DM), which is: I'd rather upgrade to business class (BC) than save 500 lives in a developing country (DC). For this reason, if some billionaire would rather upgrade his yacht than dissolve all his assets to promote communism, I don't really blame him. It seems quite a few people disagree with me, so I'm curious to see if anyone can CMV. Hello, users of CMV! This is a footnote from your moderators (MODS). We'd just like to remind you of a couple of things (COT). Firstly, please remember to read through our rules. If you see a comment that has broken one, it is more effective to report it than downvote it (DVI). Speaking of which, downvotes don't change views (DCVs)! If you are thinking about submitting a CMV yourself, please have a look through our popular topics wiki (PTW) first. Any questions or concerns (QOCs)? Feel free to message us (MU). Happy CMVing!
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::4b504a77-e4f6-447f-996a-b39d54b5: (CNN) The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels (YHR) vowed not to back down on Sunday as a top Saudi military official claimed weeks of airstrikes had significantly weakened the Shiite group (SG). "Our fighters will not evacuate from the main cities or the government institutions (GI)," rebel leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi said in a televised address (TA). "Anyone who thinks we will surrender is dreaming." His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition (SLC) bombings aimed at pushing back the YHR, who surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi (ARMH) from power. ARMH still claims he's Yemen's legitimate leader (YLL) and is working with the Saudis and other allies to return to his country. Since mid-March, more than 700 people have been killed in violence that shows no sign of slowing (NSS), according to figures from the World Health Organization (WHO). The YHR say they have the support of the country's people (CP) behind them. "It's the right of the Yemeni people (YP) to stand against the attacks in all possible means (APM) as long as the attacks continue," Al-Houthi said Sunday. "After our people move and react against the attacks and killing of children and women (KCW), we do not want to hear any voices and cries." But there are signs of some fracturing among forces loyal to former Yemeni President (FYP) Ali Abdullah Saleh (AAS), many of whom have fought alongside the rebels. Gen. AbdulRahman AlHalili, who leads more than 10,000 troops, has now allied himself with ARMH, military sources (MS) said Sunday. Meanwhile, Saudi Brig. Gen. Ahmed Asiri said Sunday that airstrikes had decimated the YHR's central command (CC) by targeting their communications. The rebels, he said, are now holding a defensive stance (DS) in besieged areas (BA). Since it began the campaign known as Operation Decisive Storm (ODS) on March 26, the SLC has launched 2,300 airstrikes, Asiri said. After hours at sea, chaos and desperation in Yemeni city. CNN's Don Melvin and Christine Theodorou contributed to this report.

Not known early Mon. if they had attorneys. Phone calls and emails to group's management team (GMT) by Associated Press (AP) not immediately returned. About dozen other suspects - all occupants of two vans - also taken into custody following concert. Information about them and charges they face not immediately available. The situation remains developing as legal proceedings continue for all involved parties detained at GSU campus following USE.

INCIDENT REPORT: Teen fatality following pursuit by law enforcement officers. Hakeem Kuta, age 17, deceased after fall from six-story structure in Bronx during police response to marijuana-related complaint. New York Police Department (NYPD) confirms subject expired Saturday AM following life support termination. Injuries sustained Thursday PM incident.

NYPD reports Kuta, student at Bronx Envision Academy (BEA), miscalculated ledge position while retreating from approaching Law Enforcement Officers (LEOs). Subject plunged six stories from residential structure rooftop.

INCIDENT BACKGROUND: LEOs responded to civilian complaints regarding Group of Teenagers (GOT) engaged in marijuana smoking and loitering activities in building lobby. Valentine Avenue location, Mott Haven district. Upon LEO arrival, Kuta plus five additional juveniles fled scene. NYPD spokesman Stephen Davis confirms officers pursued GOT up stairwell to rooftop level.

ROOFTOP SEQUENCE: Upon LEO arrival at roof level, multiple GOT members jumped to Adjacent Rooftop (AR) and successfully evaded apprehension. Kuta and 14-year-old companion (identity withheld, hereafter Companion Subject or CS) trapped by Dividing Wall (DW). Kuta attempted escape by jumping over three-foot barrier wall, failed to identify Gap Between Buildings (GBB). CS attempted rescue intervention, gripping Kuta's jacket while subject dangled 60 feet Above Ground Level (AGL) over alleyway between structures.

LEO INTERVENTION: Officer Edmundo Rivera (OER) secured CS to prevent secondary fall. Despite OER efforts, CS lost grip on Kuta. Subject fell six stories, impacting pavement in courtyard area below.

MEDICAL RESPONSE: LEOs immediately responded to Point of Impact (POI) in courtyard. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) transported Kuta to St. Barnabas Hospital (SBH) where medical staff listed condition as critical. Subject expired approximately 11:00 AM Saturday.

FAMILY STATEMENT: Father Munir Kuta, age 42, immigrant from Republic of Ghana (ROG), disputes son's involvement in Controlled Dangerous Substance (CDS) activity. Father states subject maintained clean record, avoided trouble. Quote: "It's not so easy. He was a nice kid."

ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS: NYPD authorities indicate arrest unlikely in original incident. LEO objective limited to cessation of marijuana smoking activity. No summonses issued to any GOT members. However, CDS (marijuana) recovered from building lobby, confirming initial complaint validity. Investigation continues per Standard Operating Procedures (SOP).

LOCATION DATA: Incident occurred Valentine Avenue residential building, six-story structure, Mott Haven neighborhood, Bronx. Fall occurred from Maximum Building Height (MBH) to ground-level courtyard. GBB between structures measured sufficient distance to prevent safe crossing.

WITNESS ACCOUNTS: CS (14-year-old) provided statement regarding rescue attempt and grip failure. OER filed official report documenting intervention efforts and unsuccessful outcome. Additional GOT members who escaped via AR not yet interviewed.

STATUS: Case remains open pending final Medical Examiner (ME) report and completion of Internal Affairs Bureau (IAB) review of LEO response protocols. No charges filed against surviving GOT members at this time. BEA notified of student fatality. Community outreach ongoing per NYPD Community Affairs Bureau (CAB) guidelines.

style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::6d5e183d-832b-4aa4-a6e2-563f2423: A Chinese policewoman (CPW) fought off a machete-wielding thug (MWT) with her bare hands, despite sustaining several wounds in the process. style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::23d0bd02-f2a0-4752-971c-cac75280: Person1 (P1): Hey Rocky! You've been sitting around all night. Get out and dance with someone like that Woman Over There (WOT). BULLETIN: PROGRAM CRASH CAUSES AND FAILURE MODES

Multiple factors contribute to Program Crash Events (PCE). Common PCE triggers include:

Division By Zero (DBZ): Elementary mathematics establishes that DBZ operations yield undefined results. When a program instructs the Central Processing Unit (CPU) to execute DBZ, the CPU signals an Invalid Operation Error (IOE) to the program. If the program lacks Error Handling Capability (EHC) for this IOE, a PCE occurs.

Access Violation (AV): Programs receive Memory Access Permissions (MAP) for designated Memory Address Ranges (MAR). Restricted MAR remain off-limits. When a program attempts Unauthorized Memory Access (UMA) to restricted MAR, the CPU issues an AV signal to the program. Without adequate EHC for the AV, a PCE results.

Deadlock (DL): Consider two users, User A (UA) and User B (UB), managing Resource Blocks (RB). UA possesses Red Resource Block (RRB), while UB possesses Blue Resource Block (BRB). UA initiates Resource Exchange Protocol (REP) by declaring RRB transfer contingent upon BRB receipt. UB simultaneously declares BRB transfer contingent upon RRB receipt. Both UA and UB enter Infinite Wait State (IWS), awaiting Resource Release (RR) from the other party. No Task Completion (TC) occurs. This constitutes a DL situation. When DL manifests within a program, the program enters Frozen State (FS). The only Resolution Protocol (RP) involves Process Termination (PT) followed by Program Restart (PR).

Unhandled Exception (UE): Programs frequently incorporate Exception Detection Mechanisms (EDM). When EDM identifies an error, one Program Module (PM) executes Exception Throw Operation (ETO). Another PM should execute Exception Catch Operation (ECO) to implement Error Resolution (ER). If an ETO occurs without corresponding ECO by any PM, typically an Error Dialog Box (EDB) appears, notifying users of Improper Error Management (IEM). The program then executes PT.

All these scenarios result from Software Bugs (SB) within the program. SB represent Program Code Segments (PCS) written incorrectly or lacking Complete Scenario Coverage (CSC). Some programs exhibit Higher Bug Density (HBD) than others. Contributing factors include: Development Time Constraints (DTC) imposed on Software Development Teams (SDT), Inadequate Quality Assurance Testing (QAT), or Excessive Program Complexity (EPC) making CSC extremely difficult.

Alternative conceptualization: consider a program as a Task Execution Procedure (TEP). Common TEP example: Peanut Butter and Jelly Sandwich Assembly (PBJSA). Initial TEP might specify:

Acquire bread
Acquire Peanut Butter (PB)
Acquire jelly
Acquire knife
Apply PB to Slice One (S1)
Apply jelly to Slice Two (S2)
Join S1 and S2
Execute serving

If PB supply depletion occurs mid-execution, the TEP reaches Unrecoverable State (US) with no Valid Continuation Path (VCP)—this constitutes a PCE.

More complex TEP: Pizza Restaurant Operations (PRO). PRO involves expanded Ingredient Set (IS), multiple Ingredient Combination Methods (ICM), numerous Concurrent Workers (CW) operating simultaneously, and substantially increased Potential Failure Points (PFP).

Failure categories include Recoverable Failures (RF) and Non-Recoverable Failures (NRF). NRF, along with failures developers decline to address due to Resource Allocation Decisions (RAD) or Development Priority Constraints (DPC), manifest as PCE in production environments.

BULLETIN: THANATOSIS (TH) & PREDATOR-PREY DYNAMICS (PPD)

Subjects employing TH don't exclusively simulate death. They may also secrete Foul-Smelling Liquids (FSL) indicating internal tissue has undergone Premature Decay (PD). Not all predators possess Carrion Consumption Capability (CCC), therefore target is abandoned as predator seeks Alternative Food Sources (AFS). URL0. Predators also lack Theory of Mind (ToM), preventing recognition of Deceptive Behavior Patterns (DBP).

Assessment: any animal exhibiting Disease Indicator Signals (DIS) will be avoided by predators, as Pathogen Transmission Risk (PTR) could sicken and cause Predator Mortality (PM). The animal employing Death Simulation Behavior (DSB) may appear trivial, but predator must evaluate Risk-Benefit Analysis (RBA) regarding potential ingestion of bacteria, viruses, and other Infectious Agents (IA).

Scenario: defending yourself against aggressor triggers Adrenaline Response (AR) and Extreme Defensive Behavior (EDB). When aggressor ceases Movement Activity (MA), the Threat Condition (TC) terminates and Safety Perception (SP) returns. Whether cessation results from Loss of Consciousness (LoC), death, or Feigned Immobility (FI) is irrelevant. Humans possess Cognitive Reasoning Capacity (CRC), unlike animals operating via Instinctive Response Mechanisms (IRM).

Prey Species (PS) possess Self-Protection Instincts (SPI) including trampling, headbutting, biting, goring with horns or antlers, etc. Once aggressor stops MA, the SPI abates and Interest Level (IL) decreases. Predatory Species (PrS) demonstrate similar IRM regarding prey exhibiting Escape Behavior (EB) or MA, triggering Aggression Response (AR). When prey stops MA, IL decreases except when Feeding Drive (FD) is activated.

For species like bears, which display Territorial Aggression (TA) or Defensive Aggression (DA) and disengage when TC ends, DSB proves effective. However, this strategy fails against Pack Hunters (PH) like wolves, which operate under Primary Feeding Motivation (PFM). When target ceases Resistance Behavior (RB), PH initiate Consumption Phase (CP) immediately. Strategic application of TH depends entirely on Predator Classification (PC) and Motivational State (MS).
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::a9b058a8-5ce8-448f-820a-6ffba640: Due to camera FOV (Field of View). If you're a big FPS (First Person Shooter) game player (or you know about cameras) you're probably familiar with FOV. If we consider what we can see as a cone starting at our eye and expanding out like [this] (URL0) then FOV is the angle between the two boundary lines. In FPS (First Person Shooter) games FOV is often expanded by pros to gain an advantage, since it lets you see more of your surroundings. [Here] (URL1) is a quick example of increasing a game's FOV I googled up. The image on the left has the FOV expanded to 65deg (degrees) compared to the default of 45deg on the left. With the larger FOV you can see more on the left and right. But you'll also notice that the 2 trailer things look like they're farther away even though the player is standing in the same place - that's because as you increase the FOV you also change how the light from DO (Distant Objects) is going to converge on your 2DS (Two-Dimensional Surface). Essentially a larger FOV means that objects seem to decrease in size faster as they get farther away. The opposite is also true, if you decrease the FOV then it increases the AS (Apparent Size) of FAO (Far Away Objects) since they now converge on a larger portion of the VA (View Area). The camera on DSCOVR (Deep Space Climate Observatory) used to take these pictures has a FOV of just 0.61deg. It makes it very effective at collecting light from FAO because it is focused on a very small cone. It also means that the distance between the Earth and the Moon doesn't have the same effect on RS (Relative Size) as it does when taken with a regular camera or HE (Human Eyes). Hold your hand in front of your face. It's probably about as big as your monitor. Keep your hand in the same spot and move your head backwards. Your hand now appears smaller than the monitor. There's a certain distance where your hand and the monitor get smaller together, at the same rate. This is because the distance between you and those two things becomes a lot greater than the distance between those two things. AD (Angular Diameter) depends on distance, and ROD (Ratio of Distances). Basically, the first image is very close to the moon and far from the earth, so the moon seems big. The second image is very far from both the earth and the moon, so they appear like their actual RS (Relative Sizes). So yes, the earth DOES appear smaller in the second image, but the moon got smaller a lot faster just like your hand. DSCOVR basically had its camera zoomed in more. The EPIC (Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera) camera on the spacecraft that took the image is specifically designed to observe the Earth from a distance, whereas the cameras on the AM (Apollo Missions) were more GP (General Purpose). To be more precise, in a camera the FL (Focal Length) of the lens determines the PS (Physical Size) of the image formed on the sensor. Then the PS of the sensor determines the FOV, and the PR (Pixel Resolution) of the sensor determines the size of each pixel in the image. With AF (Analogue Film) there are no pixels but the AF still has a RL (Resolution Limit) because of its chemistry and there's also a RL imposed by the lens. Finally a large image can simply be cropped, although the DSCOVR image is in fact pretty much its full size.

BULLETIN: IONIZING RADIATION (IR) AND RADIOACTIVITY (RA) OVERVIEW

Multiple radiation types exist. Light = radiation. Discussion concerns IR specifically. IR utilized in nuclear weapons (NW) and nuclear power plants (NPP).

ATOMIC STRUCTURE (AS): Atom = basic building block (BBB) of all matter. AS comprises protons, neutrons, electrons. Varying quantities/combinations = different atoms. Majority of atoms = stable (no change). Unstable atoms seek stability via offloading protons, neutrons, electrons over time. These particles expelled at high velocity = danger factor. Function as miniature projectiles impacting other matter at atomic level (AL). Upon collision with another atom, impact force sufficient to scatter target atom's protons, neutrons, etc. Comparable to pool ball striking clustered pool balls.

RADIOACTIVE DECAY (RD) PROCESS: Certain elements (CE) = unstable. To increase stability, CE release particles and energy = RA. RD occurs due to excessive particles in atom for stability maintenance. Analogy: crowded elevator (CE). Overcrowding = discomfort. Some occupants depart group rather than remaining together for complete ascent. Eventually sufficient departures occur, CE achieves comfort. Lead (Pb) formation example: uranium (U) releases sufficient particles achieving stable state, comfortable particle cohesion without loss.

RADIATION (RAD) SPECTRUM: RAD = various light types, spanning radio waves (RW) to X-rays (XR) and beyond. Some atoms = radioactive (RA-atoms), meaning decomposition occurs. During decomposition, energetic fragments expelled. One fragment type = gamma rays (GR), which = light form, therefore RAD. Early scientists discovering RA lacked complete understanding of different light types, resulting in substantial confusion regarding RAD definition, RA definition, overlap between both. Consequently, some individuals continue using RAD terminology when meaning RA.

SUMMARY DEFINITIONS:
RAD = different light types
RA = fragments expelled from RA-atoms
GR = both RAD and RA

CLARIFICATION: IR specifically references high-energy RAD capable of atomic ionization. NW and NPP both utilize IR properties. Understanding AS fundamental to comprehending RD mechanisms. Unstable atomic configurations drive particle emission. Emission velocity creates hazard through AL impacts. Historical terminology confusion persists in contemporary usage. Distinction between RAD as electromagnetic spectrum phenomenon versus RA as atomic decay process remains critical for accurate scientific communication and public understanding of nuclear technology (NT) applications and associated risks.
style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::3dd39352-d471-4ab9-bd50-b7345fc1: You can call what you're asking about a 'wealth tax' (WT), or 'capital tax' (CT). These are taxes not based on income you earned in a year, but some measure of how much you own. Some countries (Italy I believe is prime example) tax ownership of foreign land. Some countries tax amts owned by corps [Canada did this until ~5-10 yrs ago depending on prov]. Some countries strictly tax your wealth above certain level (Switzerland, as has been mentioned, does this). One form of what you are referring to that does exist in the US (United States) is the 'Estate Tax' (ET). This is tax on amt of wealth that person owns, at time they die. The threshold for when this tax applies has been very volatile over last 20 yrs, but it is generally in multi-millions, and I believe sits somewhere around $5M (five million dollars). If these taxes start to crop up more and more (and I believe they will), don't be shocked at initial 'sticker price'. Theoretically WT could replace some of current income tax (IT) regime in many countries without creating strict increased tax burden on their people. ie: if you owe $10k in IT this yr, but $2k CT is instituted next yr, then you are still in same position as long as your IT is reduced to $8k. Whether these taxes are effective/preferable or not is really question of econ (economics), not personal finance (PF), so I will not belabour that point. Note: if money you have saved earns money (interest, or divs [dividends], or maybe rent from condo you own), then those earnings are typically taxed alongside your wage income. Any 'WT/CT' as I've described it above would be in addition to IT on investment earnings (IE). Summary: WT/CT represents taxation on total assets held, distinct from standard IT on annual earnings or IE from investments.

style_bulletin_abbreviations.coling::59aec439-babf-4d21-b03b-4f331a96: First action: review T&Cs (Terms & Conditions) of CC (Credit Card), or query FI (Financial Institution), re: payment application methodology. Per Dilip's response, US FIs typically apply MP (Minimum Payment) to LRB (Lower Rate Balance), then remainder above MP to HRB (Higher Rate Balance). Other jurisdictions vary per local regs and practice. Do not assume HRB payoff or proportional allocation w/o verification. Example scenario: total debt $6000. $5000 @ 13.5% (std purchase rate), $1000 @ 22% (CAR: Cash Advance Rate). If FI applies pmts (payments) to both balances proportionally, $600 pmt reduces purchase bal by $500, CAR bal by $100. Avg APR (Annual Percentage Rate) = sum of product of APR × bal. Calculation: (.135×5000 + .225×1000)/6000 = 15%. This = WA (Weighted Average). If FI applies pmt differently—e.g., to LRB first, or specified portion to LRB with remainder to HRB—then entering this into calc (calculator) misleads, because avg APR rises over time as purchase bal pays down while CAR bal remains, or may decrease if opposite occurs. The WA methodology probably reasonably approximates circumstances described, even w/ rules applying bal differently, provided they don't 100% pay down LRB—thus simplest option for rough calcs where precision not critical, proximity sufficient. Alternative approach using online calcs: treat as two separate loans/CCs. Many calcs exist for MB (Multiple Balances). Then allocate funds differently to two 'cards'. This permits visualization of time req'd (required) until HRB payoff complete, e.g., though probably won't perfectly match actual—unless locating site w/ this specific option available, user must either accept small error in calcs or perform math manually. Summary: verify pmt application method via T&Cs or FI inquiry. US standard: MP to LRB, excess to HRB. For proportional application, use WA formula for avg APR. For differential application rules, WA provides reasonable approximation unless extreme LRB preference exists. For enhanced accuracy, utilize MB calcs treating each rate as separate CC, enabling targeted fund allocation and payoff timeline projection for HRB specifically, accepting minor variance from actual results or performing manual computation for exactitude.

style_scientific_terms.coling::dc12cc52-6173-4721-b8be-42699b3c: The accurate forecasting of temporal dynamics in complex dynamical systems (CDS) constitutes a fundamental challenge across multiple scientific disciplines. This substantial interest is nevertheless impeded by modeling challenges: frequently, the governing equations (GE) describing the underlying physics of the system under investigation are not accessible or, when known, their numerical solution may necessitate computational cost incompatible with forecasting time constraints. Consequently, approximating CDS using generic functional representations and training them ex-nihilo from available observational data has become standard practice in the machine learning (ML) era, as demonstrated by numerous successful applications utilizing deep neural networks (DNN). Nevertheless, model generalizability, uncertainty quantification margins, and the influence of training data are frequently neglected or assessed primarily through reliance on prior physical knowledge. We address these challenges from an alternative perspective by implementing a curriculum learning (CL) strategy. In CL, the training dataset is organized such that the training procedure initiates with simple samples and progresses toward increasingly complex samples to enhance convergence and generalization capabilities. This CL concept has been developed and successfully implemented in robotics and control system applications. In this work, we apply this CL concept for learning CDS in a systematic manner. Initially, utilizing theoretical foundations from ergodic theory (ET), we quantify the volume of observational data sufficient for a-priori ensuring a faithful model representation of the physical system and comprehensively examine the influence of the training set composition and its organizational structure on long-term prediction accuracy. Subsequently, we adopt entropy as a complexity metric for characterizing the training dataset; we demonstrate how informed training set design based on entropy analysis substantially enhances the resulting model performance in terms of generalization capability, and provide theoretical insights regarding the volume and selection criteria of observational data necessary for effective data-driven modeling of CDS.
style_scientific_terms.coling::7876816d-0ac2-4404-b2bf-deeaa0b7: The CII 158 micrometer spectral line constitutes the dominant coolant of the interstellar medium (ISM) in galactic systems, although significant variations in cooling efficiency are observed among different galactic systems. The primary emission mechanism at galactic spatial scales remains insufficiently characterized. Prior investigations of the CII spectral line in galactic systems employed spatial resolutions of several kiloparsecs (kpc) or greater, such that the observed emission represents a spatial average over multiple distinct ISM components. The objective of this investigation is to analyze, for the first time, the CII spectral line at the spatial scale of an individual spiral arm structure. We seek to characterize the emission mechanism of this spectral line and evaluate its utility as a star formation rate (SFR) tracer. We present CII spectral line and OI spectral line observations of a spiral arm segment in M~31 obtained using the Infrared Space Observatory (ISO). The CII emission is compared with neutral gas tracers (CO molecular line, HI atomic line) and SFR tracers (H\alpha emission line, Spitzer 24 micrometer continuum). The morphological similarity between the CII emission and the H\alpha and 24 micrometer continuum images is pronounced when convolved to identical spatial resolution, whereas the spatial correlation with neutral gas tracers proves substantially weaker. The CII cooling rate per hydrogen atom exhibits dramatic enhancement from approximately 2.7e-26 ergs/s/atom at the map periphery to approximately 1.4e-25 ergs/s/atom in SFR regions. The CII/FIR(42-122) flux ratio maintains near-constancy at 2%, exceeding typical literature values by a factor of 3. Nevertheless, we conclude that M~31 does not represent an anomalous galactic system. Rather, integrated galactic flux measurements employed in comparative analyses incorporate nuclear regions where the CII/FIR flux ratio exhibits known suppression, and spatially resolved observations neither isolate individual spiral arm structures nor extend to the galactocentric radii of the observations presented here. Fitting to published photodissociation region (PDR) models yields a physically plausible mean solution of G_0~100 and n~3000 for PDR emission in SFR regions within the M31 spiral arm structure.
style_scientific_terms.coling::1a16d27a-89fc-4df9-8b4f-cf2532a8: We investigate a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model (TBM) of a topological crystalline insulator (TCI) protected by rotational symmetry. The TBM is constructed by stacking two Chern insulators (CIs) with opposite Chern numbers which transform under conjugate representations of the rotational group, e.g. $p_\pm$ orbitals. Despite its apparent similarity to the Kane-Mele model (KMM), this TBM does not host stable gapless surface states (GSSs). Nevertheless the TBM exhibits topological responses including the appearance of quantized fractional charge (QFC) bound to rotational defects (disclinations) and the pumping of angular momentum (AM) in response to threading an elementary magnetic flux, which are described by a mutual Chern-Simons (CS) coupling between the electromagnetic gauge field (EMGF) and an effective gauge field (EGF) corresponding to the rotational symmetry. In addition, we demonstrate that although the filled bands of the TBM do not admit a symmetric Wannier representation (SWR), this obstruction is removed upon the addition of appropriate atomic orbitals (AOs), which implies fragile topology. As a result, the response of the TBM can be derived by representing it as a superposition of AOs with positive and negative integer coefficients. Following the analysis of the TBM, which serves as a prototypical example of 2D TCIs protected by rotational symmetry, we demonstrate that all TCIs protected by point group symmetries which do not have protected GSSs are either atomic insulators (AIs) or fragile phases (FPs). Remarkably, this implies that GSSs exist in free electron systems if and only if there is a stable Wannier obstruction (WO). We then use dimensional reduction (DR) to map the problem of classifying 2D TCIs protected by rotational symmetry to a zero-dimensional (0D) problem which is then used to obtain the complete non-interacting classification of such TCIs as well as the reduction of this classification in the presence of interactions.
style_scientific_terms.coling::2e921a31-8ffa-4c78-8c4d-ef7e7243: We introduce a novel artificial intelligence (AI) methodology termed the 'Digital Synaptic Neural Substrate' (DSNS). The DSNS methodology utilizes selected feature vectors from stimulus objects across multiple stimulus domains (e.g., chess problem configurations, classical musical compositions, canonical visual artworks) and performs cross-domain recombination operations on these feature vectors to generate novel feature vectors that can subsequently be utilized to synthesize novel stimulus objects possessing creative utility for human evaluators within any originating stimulus domain. This mechanism enables partial transfer of creative content synthesis burden from human agents to computational agents. The DSNS methodology underwent empirical validation within the stimulus domain of chess problem composition. We applied the DSNS methodology to automatically synthesize multiple sets of chess problem configurations based on feature vectors extracted and recombined from chess problem configurations and tournament game sequences produced by human players, canonical paintings, computer-evolved abstract visual art, photographic images of human subjects, and classical musical composition tracks. The aesthetic quality of these synthesized chess problem configurations was subsequently evaluated automatically using an existing and experimentally-validated computational chess aesthetics model (CCAM). The synthesized chess problem configurations were additionally evaluated by human domain experts. The empirical results indicate that feature vectors collected and recombined from chess stimulus domains and heterogeneous stimulus domains using the DSNS methodology can indeed be utilized to automatically synthesize chess problem configurations of reasonably elevated aesthetic quality. Specifically, a low-quality chess stimulus source (i.e., tournament game sequences between weak-rated players) utilized in combination with photographic images of human subjects successfully produced three-move chess problem configurations of comparable aesthetic quality or superior aesthetic quality relative to those synthesized using a high-quality chess stimulus source (i.e., published compositions by human domain experts), and demonstrated superior computational efficiency. The mechanism by which information from heterogeneous stimulus domains can be integrated and remain functionally viable constitutes an unresolved research question. The DSNS methodology is, theoretically, scalable and generalizable to any stimulus domain wherein stimulus objects possess feature vectors representable using real-valued numerical encodings.
style_scientific_terms.coling::28a6b262-a893-4fcb-a538-fc9aa5ad: The baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature, observed in the cosmic matter distribution at redshifts up to approximately 3.5, represents the continued expansion of the acoustic horizon initially detected in temperature anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The BAO feature position can now be determined to better than approximately 1% accuracy utilizing galaxy surveys, and approximately 1.4-1.6% precision with Lyman-alpha forests and quasar clustering. In conjunction with the Alcock-Paczyński (AP) test, which emerges from the varying ratio of angular to radial size of spherically-symmetric source distributions with distance, the BAO feature constitutes one of the most powerful observational probes for constraining the geometry of the Universe. In this investigation, we utilize five BAO feature measurements from the final data release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV (SDSS-IV), at mean redshifts <z>=0.38, 0.51, 0.70, 1.48 and 2.33, to execute a direct comparative analysis of the standard cosmological model, Lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM), and one of its principal alternative models, designated as the R_h=ct universe. For completeness, we supplement the AP test with a volume-averaged distance probe assuming a constant comoving sound horizon scale r_d. Both observational probes are independent of uncertain parameters, such as the Hubble constant H_0, and are consequently ideally suited for this type of model selection analysis. We determine that R_h=ct is favored by these measurements over the standard cosmological model based exclusively on the AP test, with a likelihood approximately 75% versus approximately 25%, while Planck-ΛCDM is favored over R_h=ct based exclusively on the volume-averaged distance probe, with a likelihood approximately 80% versus approximately 20%. A joint analysis utilizing both observational probes yields an inconclusive result, producing comparable likelihoods for both cosmological models. We are consequently unable to confirm with this investigation that the BAO feature measurements, independently, support an accelerating Universe.

Context. Filamentary structures (FS) are ubiquitous in the Galaxy, and they host stellar formation processes. Detecting FS in a reliable manner is therefore key towards our understanding of the stellar formation process.
  Aims. We explore whether supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms can identify filamentary structures across the entire Galactic plane (GP).
  Methods. We employed two variants of UNet-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image segmentation tasks. We utilized molecular hydrogen column density maps of the Galactic plane obtained with Herschel Hi-GAL observational data as input data. We trained the UNet-based CNNs with skeletal representations (spine plus branches) of filamentary structures that were extracted from these column density maps, together with background and missing data masks that we generated. We tested eight training scenarios to determine the optimal scenario for our astrophysical objective of classifying pixels as filamentary structures.
  Results. The training of the CNNs allows us to generate a novel segmented image of the Galactic plane in which pixels belonging to filamentary structures are identified. With this novel methodology, we classify more pixels (more by a factor of 2 to 7, depending on the classification threshold employed) as belonging to FS than the spine plus branches structures we utilized as input. Novel structures are revealed, which are predominantly low-contrast filamentary structures that were not detected previously. We employ standard performance metrics to evaluate the performances of the different training scenarios. This allows us to demonstrate the robustness of the methodology and to determine an optimal threshold value that maximizes the recovery of the input labelled pixel classification.
  Conclusions. This proof-of-concept investigation demonstrates that supervised machine learning algorithms can reveal filamentary structures that are present throughout the Galactic plane. The detection of these structures, including low-density and low-contrast structures that have never been observed previously, offers important perspectives for the investigation of these filamentary structures.
style_scientific_terms.coling::f4961832-eeb4-41fc-8a64-82c30107: I must preface this analysis by acknowledging my appreciation for the anime series Cowboy Bebop (CB).
